national.title: Iowa lead detonation results expected soon, EPA says
national.summary: The EPA conducted sampling at more than 130 structures in Iowa, including homes, schools, daycare centers and churches.
national.body: The Environmental Protection Agency said Thursday it expects to begin receiving sample results as early as Friday following the U.S. Army's detonation of a stockpile of degrading explosives at a munitions plant in Iowa. The EPA collected more than 1,500 air, water, soil and dust samples ahead of Wednesday's destruction of the lead azide stockpile, followed by more than 1,000 samples after the detonation, the agency said. Samples were sent to multiple EPA and private labs for testing. "The agency is expecting to start receiving lab results on post-detonation sampling as early as tomorrow," the EPA said in a news release.The EPA said it collected samples at more than 130 structures, including homes, schools, daycare centers and churches, as well as at parks, nearby farms, drinking water sources and the Mississippi River watershed.As of Thursday, no airborne lead had been detected throughout the region, the EPA said. The agency said it is also testing for other compounds that may have been released during the detonation."The agency is testing for everything we were anticipating could potentially be released as a result of the controlled detonation," it said in Thursday's news release. The Army on Wednesday detonated 5 tons of deteriorating explosives at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant located in the small community of Middletown, citing the risk of an unplanned explosion. Local residents and environmental groups had sought to block the detonation over concerns that a plume of toxic lead dust could threaten public health and agriculture. The Middletown plant housed about 10,000 pounds of lead azide, which has been used in ammunition since World War I. The EPA said the lead azide had degraded over the last 20 years it had been in storage. It had undergone a recrystallization process that increased "the material's sensitivity to friction and shock" and made it more susceptible to the "risk of unintentional detonation," the EPA said. The 8th Circuit Court of Appeals temporarily halted the detonation last week while it considered whether to impose a longer-lasting ruling. national.summary: Almost one million customers in the US had no power on Thursday evening as storms descended on both US coasts, bringing wind gusts, heavy rain and flooding.
national.body:
A massive Thanksgiving storm hammering the Midwest and north-east with heavy rain and winds, along with high tides out west, is causing widespread disruptions across the US.

More than 80 million Americans expected to be travelling this week. More than 400 flights in the US were cancelled on Thursday and another 2,200 flights into, out of, or within the US were delayed, tracking site FlightAware said.

The FAA has previously warned that delays would be possible "throughout the week" as a result of the rain and wind that are forecast.

Meanwhile, almost one million households were without power on Thursday night, with Pennsylvania, Maryland and Virginia the hardest hit states.

On Thursday, a powerful storm hit the eastern US, bringing damaging winds of up to 70mph, torrential rain, and major coastal flooding.

New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill declared a state of emergency as several communities along the Jersey Shore saw widespread flooding.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul also declared a state of emergency for New York City, Long Island and Westchester County.

In New York City, organisers of the annual Macy's Thanksgiving parade have postponed the event to Saturday.

national.title: Met Police ruined my life, says Kenyan man wrongly sentenced over attack on UK couple
national.summary: Evidence from a British police officer helped convict Ali Kololo over a 2011 attack in the Kenyan resort of Lamu.
national.body:
A Kenyan woodcutter who was wrongly sentenced to death over an attack on a British couple has told the BBC that actions by London's Metropolitan Police involved in the case destroyed his life.

Somali gunmen broke into David and Judith Tebbutt's beach bungalow on the Kenyan coast in 2011. They shot David dead and abducted Judith, holding her captive in Somalia for six months.

Met detectives flew to Kenya to assist the investigation. Their evidence helped convict Ali Kololo, who spent more than a decade in prison before his conviction was overturned.

Kololo is suing the Met, claiming a senior officer, former Detective Superintendent Neil Hibberd, gave misleading evidence at his trial and acted unlawfully to secure his conviction.

In his first media interview, he told the BBC about his 15-year ordeal and his fight for compensation, which the Met is challenging in court.

We meet on Lamu, a small island off Kenya's northern coast, once a thriving Swahili port. People and goods are still carted through its narrow stone streets by donkey rather than car.

Standing at the jetty, where police once brought him ashore in handcuffs, he relishes being free. But he is struggling to rebuild his life.

"Everything was taken from me. I'm starting from zero. I don't think I'll ever go back to who I was before," he says.

national.title: Death-sentenced Sheikh Hasina's planned return puts Bangladesh on edge - and India in a bind
national.summary: The ousted prime minister's December homecoming plan deepens Dhaka-Delhi tensions and risks fresh unrest.
national.body:
India correspondent Published 42 minutes ago Sheikh Hasina has repeatedly vowed to return to Bangladesh.

Now the ousted prime minister has put a date on her homecoming - 16 December - and even outlined how she intends to make the journey.

The government in Dhaka, which had previously dismissed the prospect, is taking her latest declaration more seriously.

Hasina, 79, who fled to Delhi in August 2024 after a student-led uprising ended her 15-year rule, plans to go back on Victory Day, the anniversary of Bangladesh's triumph over Pakistan in the 1971 liberation war, her spokesperson said.

She was sentenced to death after being convicted of crimes against humanity for her role in the crackdown, in a trial held in her absence that raised questions about due process. Her Awami League party is banned in Bangladesh. The UN says as many as 1,400 people were killed by security forces during the uprising.

The government says she would be arrested immediately if she returned and has promised to carry out the death sentence.

Hasina now wants the Bangladesh government to arrange a flight from Delhi. If that fails, she could travel commercially or cross the land border.

"She is even prepared to walk into Bangladesh," Abu Obaidha Arin, a key aide to Hasina, told the BBC.

But I invite everyone in this book to come back home to this idea of being a very special and uniquely made and divinely ordered human. There are more than 190 AKC-registered breeds assigned to one of seven groups representing characteristics and functions they were originally bred for, according to the show. Rocker won the hound group competition before advancing to the Best in Show round. Although Rocker has been crowned Best in Show 15 times, his California-based handler Mandy Clevenger was surprised by his win this year. "I just didn't expect it. It was great. What was a wonderful win," she said.Clevenger, who has handled Rocker since he started his show career at 6 months old, said the dog was energized by the crowd and "loves all the people," and he "loves all the commotion." national.title: US too focused on Middle East and not pushing Russia hard enough, Zelensky tells BBC
national.summary: Ukraine's president voices frustration with US and says it is "strange" Trump has described Vladimir Putin as a friend.
national.body:
Volodymyr Zelensky has voiced deep frustration with the US, saying that delays in delivering vital anti-ballistic missiles are costing Ukrainian lives and complaining that the US is not pushing Russia hard enough during peace talks.

In an interview with the BBC at his central Kyiv office, Ukraine's president also said it was "strange" that Donald Trump had posted a picture of himself embracing Vladimir Putin as "my friend".

"Of course it's up to the President of the United States, but... it's strange," Zelensky said, speaking in English.

"He's an aggressor, and a killer…He can't be a friend. Just cannot be," he said, suggesting it was like saying you were friends with Adolf Hitler during WWII.

Since a bruising encounter with Trump in the Oval Office in 2025, Zelensky has been careful how he handles relations with the United States.

Trump's two envoys have been trying to negotiate a peace deal between Russia and Ukraine - to end the huge loss of life. But they often seem more in tune with Moscow's position, than that of Kyiv.

The latest round of peace talks, mediated in Abu Dhabi earlier this month, made no obvious progress: "The more we know, the more problems", is how Zelensky described it.

On Thursday, Donald Trump posted on his Truth Social platform that at his own summit with Putin in China last week he had urged Russia to "pull back all military aggression against territories throughout Europe" and said he believed a peace deal with Ukraine was "a strong possibility".

national.title: Judge declines to issue a long-term ban on taxpayer-funded, pro-Trump ads critics called propaganda
national.summary: A federal judge on Wednesday sided against Democrats on the federal government's taxpayer-funded ads that promoted partisan messages and President Donald Trump ahead of the midterm elections, declining to extend a temporary ban.
national.body:
Jesse Bedayn, Associated Press Jesse Bedayn, Associated Press

NEW YORK (AP) — A federal judge on Wednesday sided against Democrats on the federal government's taxpayer-funded ads that promoted partisan messages and President Donald Trump ahead of the midterm elections, declining to extend a temporary ban.

The Democratic National Committee had argued the TV spots were illegal government-sponsored propaganda intended to promote the president's campaign message just weeks before November's midterm elections. The ruling by U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan comes after another judge in a similar case in New York also declined a long-term ban on the ads.

AliKhan noted that a previous temporary restraining order against the ads had been issued when the election was less than a week away.

"But the November 2026 midterm elections have come and gone," she wrote, adding that the DNC was now claiming the party could be harmed by the ads in December congressional runoff elections or even because the 2028 presidential cycle has already begun.

AliKhan took issue with the DNC's argument that the "permanent" nature of campaigns justified an injunction against the ads.

"Such an argument, taken to its logical conclusion, would allow the DNC to seek preliminary relief in perpetuity because it could always point to the occurrence of some election somewhere in the country," she wrote.

Democrats sued the Trump administration in October after it began airing ads that were paid for at least in part by a $20 million Department of Homeland Security contract. In court papers, the DNC challenged at least 11 government-created ads that either aired on TV or appeared on Trump administration social media feeds.

An oil tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel has capsized off the coast of Ibiza, leaving one crew member dead, authorities have said.

The six crew receiving treatment reportedly suffered minor injuries, such as hypothermia, Spanish media reports.

The possible environmental damage is being assessed by a plane and Spain's pollution control vessel, Clara Campoamor, which is owned by the country's national maritime rescue service.

"There is still little information available about a possible fuel spill," Balearic Islands' President Marga Prohens wrote on X.

Elena Delgado, maritime captain of Valencia, told news agency AFP that a small slick that had formed around the boat had "disappeared".

"The situation is stabilised," she said, adding that further inspections would be carried out on Friday morning.

Earlier, regional emergencies director Pablo Gárriz said the tanker had not completely sunk, as had originally been reported. The vessel remains partially submerged.

national.title: North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture
national.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited facilities that produce nuclear ingredients and called for building more nuclear weapons, days after ignoring U.S. President Donald Trump's offer to meet during his recent visit to Asia.
national.body:
Hyung-Jin Kim, Associated Press Hyung-Jin Kim, Associated Press

Kim Tong-Hyung, Associated Press Kim Tong-Hyung, Associated Press

SEOUL, South Korea (AP) — North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited facilities that produce nuclear ingredients and called for building more nuclear weapons, days after ignoring U.S. President Donald Trump's offer to meet during his recent visit to Asia.

Experts say Kim likely wants to show off his evolving nuclear arsenal, the backbone of his authoritarian rule, and reaffirm his rejection of any future talks on dismantling his nuclear program.

The North's official Korean Central News Agency said Thursday that Kim inspected two nuclear materials production factories, one newly inaugurated and the other being expanded. KCNA photos showed Kim and senior military officials walking between dense rows of what appeared to be centrifuges used to produce weapons-grade uranium and touring halls displaying what were believed to be warheads. Some of the images were blurred.

KCNA said Kim visited a nuclear-powered equipment production base and a nuclear research institute as well on Wednesday.

North Korea has disclosed a uranium enrichment site a few times since it showed one at its main Yongbyon nuclear complex to visiting American scholars in 2010. North Korea didn't say where the nuclear materials production factories that Kim visited this week are located. In June, when North Korea disclosed parts of a uranium enrichment site while reporting on Kim's visit there, outside experts assessed it was likely an additional uranium enrichment facility at Yongbyon.

Kim said his latest inspection visit was part of efforts to strengthen North Korea's defense capabilities in response to "variable nuclear threats approaching the Korean Peninsula moment by moment." He accused the U.S. of inciting its regional allies to possess nuclear-powered submarines and committing to sharing its nuclear weapons with them, KCNA said.

national.title: Mexico's most powerful cartels adapt as arrests and leadership battles reshape their ranks
national.summary: The arrest of another Mexican drug lord over the weekend added to a string of actions against cartels as Mexico intensifies its crackdown on organized crime under mounting pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump and with U.S. intelligence support.
national.body:
MEXICO CITY (AP) — The arrest of another Mexican drug lord over the weekend added to a string of actions against cartels as Mexico intensifies its crackdown on organized crime under mounting pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump and with U.S. intelligence support.

The capture of Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro," was hailed by both governments as a security win that may shift the balance of power within the Sinaloa Cartel. Yet violence persists among rival criminal groups across Mexico, where two powerful organizations — the Sinaloa Cartel and the Jalisco New Generation Cartel — continue to dominate the criminal landscape.

Both groups have been designated foreign terrorist organizations by the U.S., but experts say they still retain strong power in Mexico and abroad.

Here's a look at the balance of power between the two groups and how it has shifted under President Claudia Sheinbaum.

In late July 2024, two months before Sheinbaum took office, one of the Sinaloa Cartel's founders, Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada, was arrested in the U.S. following a Hollywood-esque airplane kidnapping orchestrated by "Los Chapitos," the sons of his former partner, Joaquín "El Chapo" Guzmán.

Shortly afterward, the Sinaloa Cartel plunged into a long-term internal war that continues to ravage the northern state of Sinaloa.

A year and a half later, the Mexican army killed Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes, "El Mencho," leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, or CJNG, one of Mexico's most powerful criminal groups. His death set off a violent response across 20 Mexican states that left more than 70 people dead, but it lasted only a few days.

The U.S. celebrated both operations. Zambada is serving a life sentence there, and two of his sons are cooperating with U.S. authorities. Mexico accused Washington of interference in the Zambada case although U.S. officials denied it.

national.title: Two Italians killed in strike in Kuwait, as Iran denies responsibility
national.summary: The pair were technicians for German company Rheinmetall, according to Italy's foreign ministry.
national.body:
Two Italian nationals have died following a strike on a facility in Kuwait which both countries have blamed on Iran.

The pair were technicians working for German arms manufacturing company Rheinmetall, Italy's foreign ministry said.

Iran has denied responsibility for the attack, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying the incident looked "suspicious" and that Tehran would work with Kuwait and Italy to "determine the cause".

Kuwait's defence ministry said earlier that four people - the two Italians, a Kuwaiti national and Pakistani national - had been injured from falling shrapnel after a number of drones from Iran were detected and intercepted.

It comes just over a week after Kuwait said it had repelled overnight Iranian drone attacks on an airbase which hosts US forces - the first strikes in more than two months on the country.

Recent exchanges of fire between the US and Iran, and a deadlock in negotiations, have raised fears of a major escalation in the war.

The conflict began when US and Israel attacked Iran in late February, with Iran retaliating by launching missiles and drones at Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military assets and personnel.

On Thursday, Araghchi said he had expressed condolences over the deaths in calls with his Italian and Kuwaiti counterparts and that the incident looked like a "precooked recipe for war", without expanding further.

national.title: What are king tides? These exceptionally high tides are increasingly flooding coastal communities
national.summary: King tides are the highest tides of the year, and they are increasingly flooding coastal communities as sea levels rise.
national.body:
Jennifer McDermott, Associated Press Jennifer McDermott, Associated Press

King tides are the highest tides of the year, and they are increasingly flooding coastal communities as sea levels rise.

King tide is a non-scientific or colloquial term that people often use to describe these exceptionally high tides. The 2026 super El Niño — the natural and temporary warming of parts of the Pacific — has raised coastal water levels and intensified the effects of king tides.

"Tides are incredibly complicated. Really every location has different tidal cycles and that's the basis for what a king tide is," said Alec Bogdanoff, an oceanographer and meteorologist in Fort Lauderdale, Florida. "It's a local term for the highest high tides of the year in a location. And when it impacts you, that's when they call it a king tide."

King tides typically occur when the sun, moon and Earth are nearly aligned because their gravitational pull adds together. This raises water levels and produces the greatest tidal effects of the year. This can happen on both coasts around the same time because the tides are responding to the same alignment and proximity of the moon and sun. In 2026, El Niño caused higher baseline water levels on both coasts, Bogdanoff said.

WATCH: King tides and strong waves destroy part of Pacifica pier as officials warn of coastal flooding

The highest high tides happen during full moons and new moons and seasonal cycles that can raise or lower sea levels, he added.

Historically, many coastal areas saw king tides once or twice a year, but some places are experiencing them more often than that as sea levels rise.

national.title: FCC says SpaceX can deploy 1 million satellites for data centers in space. Scientists are skeptical
national.summary: The Trump administration on Wednesday gave SpaceX the green light to deploy 1 million satellites that it said would create data centers in space, a long-lofty goal of Elon Musk's rocket company, in a move that has raised both skepticism and alarm among some scientists.
national.body:
Wyatte Grantham-Philips, Associated Press Wyatte Grantham-Philips, Associated Press

The Trump administration on Wednesday gave SpaceX the green light to deploy 1 million satellites that it said would create data centers in space, a long-lofty goal of Elon Musk's rocket company, in a move that has raised both skepticism and alarm among some scientists.

The U.S. Federal Communications Commission lauded its authorization as a historic first amid the artificial intelligence race. It said that SpaceX's one million "orbital compute modules" (forming a data center constellation called "Starmind") would process massive amounts of data that would be used back on Earth — and bring humans closer to harnessing "the full power of the sun."

"America is leading the world into the era of super intelligence," FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, who was appointed by Republican President Donald Trump, said in a statement. He added that Wednesday's move "opens a bold new frontier."

A lengthier authorization order published by the FCC noted that the company must deploy at least "one authorized space station" by 2033 — and then gradually add more and more through 2040. Musk welcomed the decision over social media.

The world's richest man has long vowed to form vast, solar-powered data centers in space to help run AI tools on Earth. But scientists and industry experts have stressed enormous technical and financial obstacles, as well as a host of environmental concerns.

Adam Becker, an astrophysicist and author, called the prospect of launching a million satellites into space to create data centers "a fantasy."

Proponents of data centers in space argue that capturing the sun's energy would ease pressure on power grids and cut demand for sprawling computing warehouses on Earth (and resources like water needed to cool them). Space seems to offer a solution because it is cold, but it is also a vacuum, trapping heat inside objects much like a thermos. Becker explained that there are "basic physical limits" to otherwise radiating that heat out — and sending lots of smaller satellites could potentially carry the necessary material combined, but it would be expensive and difficult.

national.title: 'Think twice': Banff officials issue warning over thin ice after skater's death
national.summary: After three separate incidents, one fatal, at Lake Louise, Parks Canada is warning visitors to be cautious after a warmer than average November.
national.body:
A 70-year-old local resident of Banff, Alberta, has died after falling through ice on Lake Louise, prompting warnings about outdoor safety as Canada experiences warmer than normal November temperatures.

Police said the man, who has not been identified, was ice skating alone on Tuesday evening when he fell through thin ice. He was found two hours later by a rescue team and pronounced dead at a nearby hospital.

It comes after two other ice skaters fell in the lake's frigid waters on Monday, though both survived.

Canadian park authorities have issued a warning to visitors of the world-famous Banff National Park urging them to "think twice" before stepping on the ice.

"Visitors must be able to self-rescue should they fall in the water," Parks Canada said in a notice posted on Monday.

"If you choose to skate on natural ice, you do so at your own risk."

In a statement, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police offered condolences to the 70-year-old's family. It also warned the public of the dangers of being on the ice.

Parks Canada said that early season ice can be unpredictable, and that it does not actively monitor natural ice surfaces for safety or mark potential hasards.

national.title: Analysis: Why Trump's new tariffs are less of a threat
national.summary: Other countries have rerouted trade in response to his first tariff salvo, now they are looking beyond Trump's tenure.
national.body:
There was none of last April's fanfare, the Rose Garden reveal, the gameshow blue board or "Liberation Day" rhetoric surrounding Trump's tariff announcement this week.

Instead there is something rather tentative about this latest exercise with talk of further negotiations.

"We expect to have a broad, even a plurilateral negotiation to talk about excess capacity and how to resolve it," US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC.

Around the world the view is that this week's announcement is an attempt to shore up the domestic legal underpinning of these tariffs, more than a fundamental change in the Trump trade agenda.

The tariffs are also not due to come in until January or possibly February, after a period of consultation. There has already been eight months of process and hearings, and the rates announced are upper ceilings, often up for negotiation. It's quite the contrast to the overnight shock meted out to the world last April.

Still, the US is making the argument that large swathes of the rest of the world, including allies, are harming the US goods trade position by supporting their own industries. This is the basis for the tariffs, in large part replacing the previous tariffs justified on "forced labour" provisions.

The UK, which was unaffected by the new tariff announcements, remains caught by the forced labour provisions, albeit at a rate of 10% extra on global tariffs. There was no move in response to the UK's digital services tax.

It means for many important countries there are now two legal bases upon which the Trump tariffs rest, after the Supreme Court struck down the original emergency basis earlier this year. A group of 25 states has taken the Trump administration to court to strike down the forced labour tariffs.

NEW YORK (AP) — Just over a year ago, the chief executive officer of an Ohio tech company was forced to resign when he was caught on video embracing an employee at a Coldplay concert. The CEO of McDonald's was among several pushed out over a consensual relationship at the height of the #MeToo movement.

Now the stunning reinstatement of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang despite similar allegations of sexual misconduct is fueling fears of a resurgence of impunity for the rich and powerful.

Huang resigned from Nvidia after he admitted to having an extramarital affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy, and following reports that he was involved with a second woman who was his subordinate. Huang has acknowledged that he violated the company's code of conduct, which warns against personal relationships that may create conflicts of interest.

But in an extraordinary turnaround following a pressure campaign from Huang's tech allies and President Donald Trump, Nvidia's board voted unanimously Monday to reinstate him. The board said it had received assurances from the U.S. government that Huang was not a national security concern, but there was no mention of the sexual misconduct allegations at the center of the scandal.

Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran, whose huge pop hits included "Hungry Like the Wolf," "The Reflex" and "Rio" and were inextricably linked to the launch of MTV, has died. He was 65.

Taylor's death was confirmed by his family and bandmates in a statement posted on social media and Duran Duran's website.

"From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music. His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed," the band said.

On the night he was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022, Taylor revealed that he had been battling Stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer for several years and was unable to attend.

"I would like to thank each of my brothers in this great band," he wrote. "You can dream about what happened to us but to experience it, on one's own terms, as mates, was beyond incredible."

The two-time Grammy Award-winners had nine gold records and six platinum ones, with 20 Top 20 singles in the U.K. and 18 in the U.S. They were two-time Ivor Novello Award winners and are MTV Video Visionary Award recipients.

The band's 1981 debut album "Duran Duran" had their first hit single, "Planet Earth," but it was "Rio" that transformed them into trans-Atlantic stars. The Rock Hall explained their appeal this way: "They were new wave outsiders who became music video stars — 'Tiger Beat' fashion pinups who rocked arenas."

national.body: Scammers are using AI to churn out convincing copies of real online stores, and this Black Friday, the AI agents that many shoppers will rely on often can't tell the difference.These fake sites pose a risk to the millions of Americans who are tasking their AI agents with making online purchases and transacting on their behalf. "Artificial intelligence just makes building websites so much easier. You can upload anything into HTML and build a website very, very easily," Harrison Tang, co-founder of Spokeo, a data aggregator, told CBS News.AI is enabling scammers to build what Tang described as convincing dupes of legitimate online stores in only hours, including copies of a brand's logo, marketing language and product images and descriptions."AI just makes creating these look-alike fake stores a lot easier, so there is a proliferation of them," Tang explained. "Platforms will try to catch them by not directing users there, but there are so many of them popping up all the time that they are hard to keep up with." Research from Microsoft shows that criminals can use AI to set up fraudulent e-commerce sites in mere minutes rather than the days or weeks that were once required.Spokeo identified copycat sites of dozens of popular brands, including UGG, L.L. Bean, Converse and Stella McCartney. As of Nov. 15, it had identified 65 distinct online stores that mimicked the legitimate sites of 60 brand names, according to its online shopping scam study. The discrepancies between the authentic stores and the scam websites are subtle and require close examination. The first place to look for proof of fraud, according to Tang, is in the online store's web address. For example, a fake Converse store uses the web address converseshop.us.com, whereas the real store's address is converse.com. The .us domain name is the top-level domain for the U.S. and is reserved for U.S. residents, but is commonly used for phishing attempts, according to Tang. "It looks like an official website, but it's not, so if you don't pay close attention, it's easy to get tricked," he said. AI agents need to get savvyBots aren't as well trained as some humans are at spotting phony websites, which can dupe even discerning shoppers because of how realistic they look. national.title: Elon Musk doubles SpaceX share pledge for U.S. children
national.summary: Every child in the U.S. will receive one share of SpaceX from the company and one from Elon Musk.
national.body: Elon Musk is upping a pledge to kickstart U.S. children's savings. On Wednesday, Musk and SpaceX said they will give every U.S. child two shares in the space exploration company, doubling a pledge the world's richest person made in October, which he said at the time would be the "first of many" planned gifts. In the statement, SpaceX said it would give each child a newly issued share of its Class A common stock. The company will contribute the shares to U.S. kids' Trump Accounts, tax-advantaged investment accounts the White House created to help American children build long-term savings. Musk will personally match the number of shares SpaceX donates, according to Thursday's statement. Additionally, SpaceX president and chief operating officer Gwynne Shotwell will donate more than 2 million SpaceX shares to U.S. children.The total giveaway is worth about $18 billion, based on SpaceX's most recent stock price. "SpaceX is building the infrastructure of the future and working to make life multiplanetary," the company said in announcing the donation. "We believe ownership of the company creating these systems should extend to the next generation of Americans for their long-term benefit."There are roughly 70 million children in the U.S. who are eligible for a Trump Account. The Trump administration is automatically enrolling kids under eighteen with a valid Social Security number in the program. However, parents or guardians must still claim their child's account for it to be active. As of Tuesday, friends and family members had contributed more than $1 billion to individual Trump Accounts, according to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. Additionally, philanthropists including Michael and Susan Dell and other donors have made major gifts, bringing the total assets deposited in Trump Accounts to over $9 billion.

national.title: French cinema star Gérard Depardieu ordered to stand trial for rape and sexual assault
national.summary: Gérard Depardieu, for decades one of France's most celebrated actors, has been ordered to stand trial on charges of raping and sexually assaulting a young actress, authorities said Thursday, less than two weeks after the cinema star abandoned his appeal of a sexual assault conviction in a separate c
national.body:
Thomas Adamson, Associated Press Thomas Adamson, Associated Press

PARIS (AP) — Gérard Depardieu, for decades one of France's most celebrated actors, has been ordered to stand trial on charges of raping and sexually assaulting a young actress, authorities said Thursday, less than two weeks after the cinema star abandoned his appeal of a sexual assault conviction in a separate case.

Actress Charlotte Arnould was 22 when she accused Depardieu in 2018 of raping her at his Paris home.

Eight years later, the Paris Court of Appeal ruled that the actor should face trial over allegations of rape and sexual assault on Aug. 7, 2018, while dismissing allegations relating to a second incident six days later.

Depardieu, 77, has denied the rape allegations. His lawyer, Delphine Meillet, told The Associated Press that he disputes Thursday's ruling, without specifying whether he would challenge it before France's highest court for civil and criminal cases.

The ruling upholds part of an investigating judge's August 2025 decision to send Depardieu to trial.

The case has become one of the most prominent in France's reckoning with sexual violence, as the #MeToo movement has faced resistance in the country, particularly in the arts.

With his hulking frame, crooked nose and commanding screen presence, Depardieu dominated French cinema for half a century.

national.summary: President Donald Trump, who has staked his economic policy on growth in the artificial intelligence sector, will travel to Arizona on Dec. 4 to speak at the groundbreaking for a new Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. computer chip foundry, according to both the White House and the Taiwan-based c
national.body:
WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (AP) — President Donald Trump, who has staked his economic policy on growth in the artificial intelligence sector, will travel to Arizona on Dec. 4 to speak at the groundbreaking for a new Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. computer chip foundry, according to both the White House and the Taiwan-based company.

The trip will come at the end of a week where AI comes under the microscope in Washington in the aftermath of Trump intervening to get his ally Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO of Nvidia. Huang is slated to testify at a Senate Banking Committee hearing on Dec. 3 and will face questions about how his company has been selling its chips abroad — and his affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Beijing has denied it.

WATCH: How Trump may have profited from Huang's return to Nvidia

TSMC has expanded aggressively in the Phoenix, Arizona, area, using its U.S. facilities to manufacture chips for tech companies such as Nvidia, Apple, AMD, Broadcom, and Qualcomm. Trump is attending the start of construction on the fifth phase of TSMC's expansion in Arizona.

TSMC in July announced plans to spend another $100 billion on expanding its manufacturing capacity in the United States, bringing its total pledged investment in American chipmaking to $265 billion.

WATCH: U.S. works to close loophole that let China access advanced AI chips

The size of the investment has grown as the development of artificial intelligence has stimulated demand for more computer chips, at the same time as Taiwan's dominance in chipmaking has led countries including the U.S. to address supply chain vulnerabilities by producing more domestically.

While Trump has sought to promote the investments as a function of his tariffs, the company began construction in Arizona during the presidency of Democrat Joe Biden. The bipartisan CHIPS and Science Act, signed into law by Biden, also helped to provide some financial support for the project.

KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Russia is preparing another major attack on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, logistics and critical services, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Thursday, as U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said Russian President Vladimir Putin has "shown restraint" in the war by agreeing not to use nuclear weapons.

Kushner, who is mediating Russia-Ukraine talks with envoy Steve Witkoff, said that after talking at length with Putin, he believes the Russian leader wants peace almost five years after Moscow invaded Ukraine.

Putin "has agreed not to use nuclear weapons, which obviously is a big thing, and he's reassured us that that's not his intention," Kushner said on the MD Meets podcast by Axel Springer Creators.

The son-in-law of U.S. President Donald Trump added that "what (Putin) is saying is peace, but I think it's always peace on what terms" as the talks have hit "a little bit of a deadlock" over the fate of Ukrainian territory.

Zelenskyy and European leaders have criticized Putin for what they describe as Moscow's refusal to compromise and determination to press on with an invasion that has killed hundreds of thousands of troops and thousands of Ukrainian civilians.

Putin wants a new relationship with Washington, according to Kushner, as Russia seeks to keep NATO away from its borders.

national.title: Trump calls GDP figures 'fake' and demands an investigation of Commerce Department
national.summary: President Donald Trump on Thursday accused his Commerce Department of purposely issuing incorrect economic growth figures before the midterm elections, and said he wants to launch an investigation.
national.body:
WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (AP) — President Donald Trump on Thursday accused his Commerce Department of purposely issuing incorrect economic growth figures before the midterm elections, and said he wants to launch an investigation.

Trump has repeatedly sought to undermine trust in economic data that fails to match his claims of a historic boom, a pattern that threatens the credibility of figures needed by businesses, financial markets and consumers when making investments.

His latest complaint concerns data issued by the Commerce Department on Wednesday that revised gross domestic product in the third quarter to 4.3% on an annual basis, up from a prior estimate of 3.4%.

The department's Bureau of Economic Analysis routinely updates its economic data to improve their accuracy. GDP figures, monthly jobs reports and other data are regularly revised. Those updates occur on a pre-scheduled basis without regard to the political calendar.

But the president claimed on social media that it was a "massive, and purposeful, error" and linked it to the poor performance for Republicans in the Nov. 3 midterm elections that gave Democrats control of both houses of Congress.

"It was just revealed that the REAL Numbers on the Economy, published before the Election, were FAKE, and a correction was issued yesterday by the people in the Government Agency that does these numbers," Trump posted. "Why wasn't the correct number issued before the Election? I am asking for an immediate investigation of this situation."

WATCH: How Trump's newest tariffs could impact Americans and the economy

The Commerce Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The government is largely closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday.

national.title: Nine injured, three critically, after Bangkok oil refinery explosion
national.summary: Black smoke could be seen across Bangkok's skyline after the blast, as officials urged residents to leave the area.
national.body:
Nine people have been injured after an explosion at an oil refinery in Bangkok, authorities have said.

Three of them are in critical condition, according to news agency AFP, which said the local hospital had revised its earlier assessment of four.

A fire broke out after the blast at the Phra Khanong facility run by energy giant Bangchak Corporation in the east of Thailand's capital at around 14:45 (07:45 GMT).

The company said the fire was brought under control and put out within 30 minutes, adding that the cause of the incident was being investigated.

Black smoke could be seen across Bangkok's skyline after the blast, as local officials told residents to leave the area.

An alert sent to mobile phones by Bangkok authorities confirmed that the fire was under control, but urged people to avoid the area.

Eyewitnesses shared video clips on social media of flames and smoke rising above the refinery.

On a visit to the scene, Thailand's energy minister Akanat Promphan said it appeared the impact of the explosion was limited because the fire started in a distillation tower about 100m (330ft) from where oil was being stored.

national.title: Could the Black Sea pull the U.S. into war in Europe?
national.summary: The Russia-Ukraine war is spilling into the Black Sea, where violent incidents have surged, running right up to NATO's doorstep.
national.body: Constanța, Romania – Out on the Black Sea, the Romanian Navy is always on the lookout for the deadly debris of a war it isn't fighting.It's a front of the Russia-Ukraine war that most people rarely see. It runs right up to NATO's doorstep and sometimes crosses into its waters — threatening to pull the alliance, and therefore the United States, into the war.Incidents involving drones, mines and commercial ships are surging in the Black Sea, NATO military spokesperson Colonel Martin O'Donnell told CBS News."In 2025, for example, we saw fewer than 50 incidents in the Black Sea. This year alone, we're talking four to five hundred," he said.The roughly tenfold increase threatens a major artery of global grain and fuel shipments and has made the waterway deadlier than the Strait of Hormuz, a flashpoint in the U.S.-Iran war, with both sides trying to enforce blockades on the chokepoint to exert economic pressure on the other.Twenty-five sailors have been killed in the strait this year, according to the International Maritime Organization, while at least 40 have been killed in the Black Sea in the same period, according to the International Transport Workers' Federation."I would say the Black Sea is just as important, and then depending on who you talk to, some might argue could perhaps even be more important … in terms of global trade," said O'Donnell.Any imbalance in the flow of fuel and food "can have global implications that can impact America just as much as it can any of the nations here," he said.And this maritime front stretches beyond the Black Sea.Over the weekend, Ukraine said it struck an advanced Russian warship and a cargo ship that then drifted, on fire, into the waters of NATO member Finland.On Sunday, Ukraine said it sank a Russian warship docked in Libya.Three of the six countries bordering the Black Sea are NATO members — Romania, Bulgaria and Turkey.But as Romanian Navy Captain Mihai Iordache explains, defending those borders is nothing like defending them on land."We do not have a fence into the Black Sea to state this is our border, that is the other border," he said.The Romanian Navy is deploying highly specialized divers and drones, scouring the depths for unexploded weapons.All this comes as the pressure on NATO is mounting. national.title: Judge blocks FCC from early license review for ABC, which network says has had a chilling effect
national.summary: A federal judge on Wednesday blocked the Federal Communications Commission from conducting an early review of ABC's broadcast licenses, agreeing with the network that the Trump administration was chilling the network's free speech rights.
national.body:
Michael Kunzelman, Associated Press Michael Kunzelman, Associated Press

WASHINGTON (AP) — A federal judge on Wednesday blocked the Federal Communications Commission from conducting an early review of ABC's broadcast licenses, agreeing with the network that the Trump administration was chilling the network's free speech rights.

U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan in Washington, D.C., granted ABC's request for a temporary restraining order and a preliminary injunction on First Amendment grounds. The network accuses the FCC of violating its free speech rights in retaliation against programming decisions that the Trump administration dislikes.

AliKhan noted in her ruling that the network was likely to succeed on its First Amendment claim.

AliKhan, who was nominated by former President Joe Biden, said ABC had detailed "a campaign of retaliation against them in response to their exercise of their First Amendment rights," which on its own is an 'irreparable injury.'"

ABC and its parent company, Disney, sued the FCC and FCC Commissioner Brendan Carr in August, several months after the commission ordered eight ABC-owned stations to submit renewal applications for their broadcast licenses years ahead of schedule.

"Today's decision is an important victory for the First Amendment," a spokesperson for ABC News said in a statement.

An FCC spokesperson said in a statement that the part of the decision granting ABC's motion "is wrong on the facts and wrong on the law," adding that the agency "looks forward to prevailing in full on this matter."

local.title: 'A Buffalo Tradition': 131st annual Turkey Trot runs a new route
local.summary: More than 14,000 runners took on a new circular route for Buffalo's 131st annual YMCA Turkey Trot this Thanksgiving.
local.body: More than 14,000 runners took on Buffalo's 131st Annual YMCA Turkey Trot Thursday, and this year they faced a brand new route. The race is a highlight of Buffalo's running calendar and a Thanksgiving tradition dating back to 1896. But this year runners lined up behind a new downtown start line as the 5-mile race took a new circular route. Previously a point-to-point route, the new course was created this year after the former start point, the Delaware Avenue branch of the YMCA, closed down.Runners and walkers of all ages and abilities took to the course Thursday, including a few canine companions. Christopher Bertola of Orchard Park was the first to cross the finish line, with a time of 24:14. He gave the new route a thumbs up. "I like it honestly, it's a fast course, it's flat," Bertola said. "Being local, it's a race I've heard about my whole life—it's always been a goal of mine to go out and win it."Gabrielle Orie from Buffalo was the first female to finish, with a time of 27:12. She was thrilled to win on home turf."It doesn't get better than a Turkey Trot in your hometown running in the streets where you grew up in," Orie said."Honestly the new route is a bit of a grind," Orie added.Though change can be tough, some traditions remain. Weary runners headed into the Buffalo Convention Center for a post-race drink or two before heading home for a Turkey dinner.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. Our editorial team verifies all reporting on all platforms for fairness and accuracy.

local.title: Buffalo family behind Blizzard of '77 game releases limited 50th anniversary edition
local.summary: The family behind the Blizzard of '77 Travel Game is bringing back this unique piece of Buffalo history to commemorate the upcoming 50th anniversary of those five fateful winter days.
local.body: The family behind the Blizzard of '77 Travel Game is bringing back this unique piece of Buffalo history to commemorate the upcoming 50th anniversary of those five fateful winter days.On the morning of January 28, 1977, just after 11 a.m., the blizzard began. Over the next few days, Buffalo and surrounding areas saw snow fall as high as 100 inches, with high winds creating drifts as high as 30 to 40 feet. The weather was so severe that President Jimmy Carter declared an "emergency" for the entire states of New York and Pennsylvania, the first time a snowstorm had prompted such a response.At the time, Buffalo resident Paul Marino was only nine years old."My dad, he was a salesman, and we were living in Buffalo, and he drove down to Jamestown the morning of the blizzard," Paul told WKBW. "He was coming back from his morning appointment. Around 11:10 a.m. is when the storm actually struck."According to Paul, his father, Chuck Marino, found the thruway route impassable. Attempting to turn around, Chuck found a handful of other motorists who had been stranded due to the worsening conditions. Eventually, he and the other travelers took refuge from the storm at a fire station in Irving for two days."During that time, we (Paul and his mother Donna) would check in with him; he'd give us a call, and he was explaining to us, Mom and I, what that experience was like trying to drive that." Paul continued, "My parents always loved playing games with me; they always encouraged creativity, so I took one of my dad's legal pads, and he hated when I did this, but I ripped off all of the paper so I could have the cardboard, right? I've got the cardboard, I grabbed some of my markers and my Matchbox cars."Paul would go on to draw a road, including snow drifts, abandoned cars, dead batteries, and other obstacles his father had witnessed firsthand. When Chuck returned home and saw his son's creation, that moment inspired the Blizzard of '77 Travel Game.The original Blizzard of '77 Travel Game moved remarkably quickly from idea to market. Released in July 1977, the first production run of 40,000 games sold out almost immediately. A second run followed, bringing total sales of the original Buffalo edition to more than 70,000 games.Following these initial releases, no further copies of the game would be made. local.summary: Screenwriter Ryan March says production is targeting fall 2027, with a Christmas 2028 theatrical release.
local.body: The extraordinary story of a Western New York man who helped rescue dozens of people during the 2022 Christmas Blizzard is headed to the big screen.The feature film, titled "Merry Christmas, Jay," is moving through pre-production, with plans to shoot in Buffalo in September and October 2027.Screenwriter and producer Ryan March told 7 News that the production is targeting a theatrical release around Christmas 2028.March first learned about Jay Withey's actions while watching national news coverage of the historic blizzard from his home in Los Angeles. A former college roommate who had lived in Western New York called to ask whether he thought the story could become a movie.March's response was immediate."I said it's gonna be a movie. He explained that he had been stranded with two other people in his truck and discovered seven elderly people who were also stuck and running out of fuel."I had to do it to save everyone and get them to shelter, food, and a bathroom," Withey wrote.The film has been in development for more than three years. March said the production is now casting and working to finalize arrangements with New York State and Western New York for film incentives, locations and crew.Much of the crew is expected to come from Buffalo and the surrounding region.March said his team has been approached by other potential filming locations, including Atlanta, New Mexico, Canada, the United Kingdom, Romania and Bulgaria. The Genesee Brewery is partnering with Foodlink for the first time to turn its annual Keg Tree lighting into a food drive.

The first 200 people who arrive to the event on Dec. 4 with three non-perishable food items will receive a free mug, shaped like a keg and etched with a picture of the Keg Tree. The food drive will continue through the holiday season at the Genesee Brew House.

Mark Dwyer at Foodlink said the event comes at a pivotal time for food insecurity in Rochester.

"It's a great chance to just raise awareness locally for not only Foodlink and the work that we do, but just the issue of food insecurity that impacts thousands of our neighbors," Dwyer said.

Foodlink tracks data from all of the food pantries in its network around the region. Dwyer said that the numbers of people visiting food pantries from August and September were the highest the nonprofit has ever seen. Those months also saw a 13% increase in food pantry usage compared to the previous year.

"What's on everyone's mind: food, fuel, prices are sky high," Dwyer said. "Just inflation and the economy are continuing to impact people's ability to put food on the table."

The Genesee Brewery approached Foodlink to partner at Keg Tree. Carl Falk, general manager for the Genesee Brew House, said the plan is to focus the company on giving back to the Rochester community.

"Foodlink has been such a staple in our community, helping people, and obviously this time of year there's an even greater emphasis on being a community partner," Falk said.

local.summary: Another round of proposals to close some Buffalo Public Schools is back on the table — one submitted by the interim schools superintendent and another put forward by some board members.
local.body: Another round of proposals to close some Buffalo Public Schools is back on the table — one submitted by the interim schools superintendent and another put forward by some board members.Interim Schools Superintendent Dr. Ebony Prophet-Bullock submitted the district's plan, tweaked from the original that was voted down. It proposes to close the Early Childhood Center, the Bilingual School, Drew Science, Riverside Academy, PS 131 Academy School and East Community High School. However, it no longer includes changes for Middle Early College.“The superintendent's first plan was not a bad plan, just over time, it got really, really muddy up,” stated Erik Bohen, Park District School Board Member.“We have to make sure we do this right and do it well.”But four board members submitted their own proposal. It calls to keep the Early Childhood Center, the Bilingual School and Drew Science open, and instead calls to close the Marva J. Daniel Futures School in the city's Fruit Belt.“The issue is though -- we are running out of money, and we will not have money next year,” declared Bohen.Bohen told me the board could vote Monday night during a special session."I believe 95-percent certain that that will get done," Bohen remarked. “What makes you so confident that it could be done on Monday?” Buckley asked. “Just from my talking's with other board colleagues, I believe no one’s telling me how they're voting but, I believe everybody has their mind made up of where we go, and I believe they've also had pressure from the community as well to get this done," replied Bohen.Both plans still call to phase out Riverside High School.Riverside social studies teacher Marc Bruno told me he doesn't trust the process."This process has been a train wreck from the day it started," Bruno commented. "The trauma that this is putting our students and staff under is unbelievable.”Bruno is questioning the timing of Monday's special meeting."The fact that they announce that there's a special meeting right after we leave for Thanksgiving break on the Monday we get back from break. local.title: 'Make-or-break': Buffalo businesses prepare for Small Business Saturday
local.summary: Small businesses along Buffalo's Elmwood Avenue are gearing up for what they hope will be a big weekend for local shopping.
local.body: Small businesses along Buffalo's Elmwood Avenue are gearing up for what they hope will be a big weekend for local shopping.Small Business Saturday is this weekend, serving as a community-driven counterpoint to the retail push of Black Friday.I spoke with several Elmwood Village business owners. Tracey Wei, who owns zero-waste home and body care store Little Salmon, described the area as "welcoming and walkable."Wei told me independent businesses like hers often rely on Small Business Saturday to stay afloat."This weekend is like make-or-break for the last quarter," Wei said.Like many businesses in the neighborhood, she'll be holding a sale on Saturday to promote more foot traffic."Businesses need your money more than billionaires, so every dollar you spend, like 70-80% of it stays with the community," she said.WATCH: 'Make-or-break': Buffalo businesses prepare for Small Business SaturdayOther owners pointed to the unique experience shoppers find in the neighborhood."There are many unique shops you're not gonna find somewhere else, and you get better customer service," Wendie Reed said.At Reed's consignment store, Scoop Shop, shoppers might even find an outfit for the World's Largest Disco on Saturday at the Buffalo Convention Center.Small Business Saturday is one of many events being held to bring people to the area. Seamus Gallivan, the new executive director of the Elmwood Village Association, said the density of the neighborhood is part of its appeal."The beautiful thing about this neighborhood is there are so many businesses so close together that however you get here, you can stay on foot for hours and find everything you need and more," Gallivan explained. He said the stores will also participate in a Christmas window display competition starting December 5. For now, the focus is on bringing people out this Saturday. The day carries real weight for the neighborhood's businesses, said Christa Penner, who owns ShopCraft. "It's a huge day for us, and it's really important that other members of the community come out and support the small businesses in your neighborhoods," Penner said.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. local.title: Concerns raised over conditions at cemetery between Colden and Holland
local.summary: Overturned headstones, fallen tree limbs and overgrown vegetation are raising concerns about a cemetery between Colden and Holland.
local.body: Overturned headstones, fallen tree limbs and overgrown vegetation are raising concerns about a cemetery between Colden and Holland.Jeffrey Smith contacted me after visiting the cemetery and becoming concerned about what he found. He said the grounds have not been properly maintained, leaving some burial sites partially obscured by vegetation and debris.“Everything when it was green this summer, you couldn't even see part of these stones because the growth was bad,” Smith said. “And now the leaves and limbs are all over the place.”Smith also pointed to a large tree limb that had fallen near burial sites, raising concerns about the potential for additional damage to headstones.“The big limb just came down over there this year apparently,” he said. “This was here in the spring when we came up and checked.”Smith said veterans are among those buried at the cemetery and believes their graves deserve better care.“All these veterans have served our country," he said. "We should be taking care of their graves." WATCH: Concerns raised over conditions at cemetery between Colden and Holland7 News contacted the Town of Colden to figure out who is responsible for maintaining the property. Documents show that the cemetery is privately owned.Town officials said Scouts sometimes volunteer to help clean up the grounds.7 News also contacted the property owner for comment about the cemetery's condition but did not receive a response. Smith lives nearly two hours away and said he cannot regularly visit to monitor the property. He hopes someone will take action.“I'd like to see it cleaned up, maintained, lawn mowed and for it to look proper,” Smith said.He hopes the cemetery can be restored to a condition that is respectful to the people buried there and the families who come to visit.

entertainment.title: The Best Thanksgiving TV Episodes and Movies to Binge Right Now
entertainment.summary: "Pass the Turkey." There's certainly a high chance you've heard a family member make that infamous request once everyone has gathered around the table for Thanksgiving, a time filled with...
entertainment.body:
There's certainly a high chance you've heard a family member make that infamous request once everyone has gathered around the table for Thanksgiving , a time filled with aforementioned turkey and stuffing yourself with the requisite mashed potatoes, pumpkin pie and a whole lot of awkward small talk with those distant family members you see about as often as you go to the dentist.

"I know, I can't believe it's been so long." "Yes, I'm still single." "No, I haven't watched The Studio yet."

And that's why you need comfort food. No, we're not talking about Aunt Maureen's green bean casserole and the rest of the feast you're impatiently waiting to dive into, we're talking about comfort food for your soul that only a treasured TV show or movie can provide.

So if you're looking for a cozy distraction right now, we've rounded up some of our favorite Thanksgiving-themed episodes of shows like Gossip Girl , How I Met Your Mother and Friends (could the NBC series be any better at celebrating the football-and feast-focused holiday), as well as a few movies about Turkey Day.

Yes, there are actually plenty of films made about the Jan Brady of holidays, even if Halloween and Christmas tend to gobble up the majority of the attention at the end of each year.

Some are more showy about it (see: Planes, Trains & Automobiles ) while others just make a passing reference, but thanks to that scene in Zabar's (featuring a pre- Grey's Anatomy Sara Ramirez ) we want You've Got Mail to be a Thanksgiving movie, we want it so badly.

So, stockpile a plate of leftovers, hibernate in the basement and get ready to stream your long weekend away.

entertainment.title: The Hunting Wives Creator Defends Major Season 2 Death: 'It's Important That Things Have Consequences'
entertainment.summary: The second season of Netflix's The Hunting Wives loses a major character in Episode 5. Creator Rebecca Perry Sutter tells TVLine why it had to happen.
entertainment.body:
Netflix Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Warning: This interview spoils a major twist from "The Hunting Wives" Season 2, Episode 6. Proceed at your own risk.

Now streaming on Netflix, the second season of "The Hunting Wives" takes the ladies Maple Brook, Texas on another deadly thrill ride — and not everyone makes it out alive. The biggest death of the season, and arguably the series, occurs in Episode 6. It's shocking, it's upsetting, and like most tragedies on this show, it involves Margo.

Malin Akerman's character returns home from a chaotic church service, only to find Brad waiting in her living room. She knows that he's unwell — the entire congregation watched him interrupt the service in a hospital gown, begging his father for help — but she doesn't know exactly what went down behind closed church doors, including that Brad shot his father for picking up the police's phone call.

Brad puts down the gun long enough to have a civilized catch-up with his former lover, but that doesn't mean Margo likes what she hears. New information has Brad questioning whether his mother really killed Abby last season, and when when he remembers hearing Margo mention an abortion, he puts two and two together, concluding that Margo is the killer.

In a very "Chicago" moment, both Margo and Brad reach for the gun, but Margo gets her hands on it first, shooting Brad dead in her own home. Naturally, Sophie comes to Margo's rescue, agreeing to tell the police that Brad was shot in self-defense.

"R.I.P., Baby Brad!" series creator Rebecca Perry Cutter tells TVLine, explaining that she wrote Brad's dramatic downfall in Season 2 because she knew that actor George Ferrier "could do more than he did in Season 1," which he absolutely proved in these six episodes.

And while many viewers are likely disappointed to lose this lovable mess, Cutter believes that Brad's death was a necessary road bump in the Hunting Wives' collective journey .

"I think it's important that things have consequences," Cutter says. "He is kind of the biggest living victim of Season 1 because his girlfriend was murdered, and his mom was murdered and blamed for being a murderer. Margo did this to him, so I think it was important to let the reality of that exist. We wanted to show that, yeah, he got f***king traumatized, and then his father can't deal with him, and he's shipped away, and s**t goes bad. That was just something that we were really interested in seeing."

entertainment.summary: Olivia Rodrigo's "stupid song" video was filmed at the beloved store with its infamous tabby Oliver.
entertainment.body:
There’s some fierce competition over a feline adoption on the Upper West Side, and we’re not kitten you.

Beloved local grocer Zingone Bros. on Manhattan’s Upper West Side is closing after nearly 100 years , leaving its famed bodega cat Oliver, who starred in an Olivia Rodrigo music video, looking for a new home.

The opportunity is proving to be catnip for Rodrigo fans, and there’s an avalanche of interest in adopting the orange tabby, who became a star after she filmed the music video for “stupid song,” at the store last spring.

The feline was outfitted with a GoPro camera, and his paws can be seen throughout.

J.J. Grabenstein, a longtime customer at the shop who takes Oliver to the vet and generally cares for him, is now in charge of finding his purr-fect future family.

“I was up till midnight answering emails,” she tells Page Six. “Some people know him from the video, and some know him from the store.”

The inquiries from fans of the “drop dead” singer have come in from far-flung states, says Grabenstein, who has other pets and will be fostering the cat while she searches for the perfect adoptive family. “He should be the only pet in the home because he is the star,” she tells us.

entertainment.title: Steelers owner picks a side in Aaron Rodgers and coach Mike McCarthy’s nasty public feud
entertainment.summary: The team owner said it was the right move to cut Rodgers after his recent "insubordination."
entertainment.body:
It’s safe to say Aaron Rodgers won’t be getting a gift from his former boss this holiday season.

Pittsburgh Steelers owner Art Rooney II made it crystal clear that he’s in Mike McCarthy’s corner amid the head coach’s explosive feud with the quarterback — saying Rodgers’ actions this week were out of bounds.

“I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond,” Rooney told the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette .

“The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization,” he continued. “When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.”

Rodgers — who previously stated this would be his final NFL season — was cut by the Steelers Wednesday, shortly after he gave a jaw-dropping assessment of his reunion with McCarthy on the “Pat McAfee Show.”

During the interview, Rodgers claimed the coach — with whom he won a Super Bowl as a member of the Green Bay Packers in 2011 — was falling asleep during meetings, was “unhealthy” and broke a huddle by saying the wrong team’s name .

McCarthy later claimed Rodgers presented an ultimatum over play-calling duties , telling him to either hand the reins to someone else or release him.

Rodgers’ appearance on the ESPN show came after he found out through teammate Pat Freiermuth that he lost his starting gig to backup quarterback Mason Rudolph. His words have since been slammed by many, including his former Packers teammate T.J. Lang .

entertainment.title: Anuel AA’s ‘RHLM2’ Album Is Finally Here: ‘I Made It With My Heart and Soul’
entertainment.summary: The long-awaited album is a sequel to his 2018 debut, Real Hasta La Muerte, and his first in four years.
entertainment.body:
Anuel AA is celebrating his 34th birthday on Thursday (Nov. 26) with the release of his long-awaited RHLM2 album.

The sequel to his debut studio album, Real Hasta La Muerte (2018), is home to 23 tracks that blend trap and reggaetón. It’s a return to the sound that made him a household name as “El Dios del Trap” (The God of Latin Trap).

Though it’s taken the Puerto Rican act nearly 10 years to release the sequel to RHLM — which debuted at No. 1 on Top Latin Albums in July 2018—he has released other promising albums in between, including Emmanuel (2020) and Las Leyendas Nunca Mueren (2021), both of which also hit No. 1 on the chart.

“I poured my heart and soul into this album for everyone who believes in me and stays loyal no matter what. This album means the world to me. There are no perfect words to explain how I feel and what I feel for this album,” he said in an Instagram post ahead of the set’s release on Thanksgiving night. He dedicated his new project to his fans, his family and those who have stuck by his side during the good and bad times.

He continued: “Thank you for never giving up on me, I love you all so much with all my heart!!!!!!! I made this album for you […] I will never forget you!!!!!”

From trapsoul to sensual reggaetón, RHLM2 includes fiery collaborations such as “Sexo Nama” with De La Rose, “Tal Ve Un Ignorante Fui” with ROA and “Si Me Matan a Balazos” with Fuerza Regida. Most notable is “Instagram,” a collaboration with Blessd and Wisin, where they cleverly sample Don Omar’s 2006 hit “Myspace” alongside Wisin y Yandel.

The set wraps with five previously released commercial hits—“Amanece” feat. Haze (2018), “Mas Rica Que Ayer” feat. Mambo Kingz & DJ Luian (2022), “¿Qué Nos Pasó?” (2022), “La Llevo al Cielo” feat. Chris Jedi, Chencho Corleone & Ñengo Flow (2022) and the Ovy on the Drums-produced “Deportivo” feat. Blessd (2024)—further reminding fans of his ongoing star power.

entertainment.title: Watch Miranda Lambert Perform Medley of Her Hits at Dallas Cowboys Halftime Show
entertainment.summary: The native Texan tackled songs like "Gunpowder & Lead" and "Little Red Wagon" in her first NFL appearance during the annual Thanksgiving tradition
entertainment.body:
You can tell that Miranda Lambert is from Texas, but, until today, she’d never performed for her hometown football team — or anyone in the NFL , for that matter. Singing a medley of her classic hits (which she affectionately called “bangers and mash,” i.e., a mashup of her bangers), Lambert made her halftime show debut during the Thanksgiving Day matchup between the Dallas Cowboys and the Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium.

Following a pretaped introduction by Reba McEntire, who announced Lambert as the “most awarded artist in the history of the Academy of Country Music,” the Grammy-winning singer took the stage to perform “Snakeskin Boots” (sorry, no Ella Langley cameo), “Kerosene,” “Gunpowder & Lead,” “Mama’s Broken Heart,” and “Little Red Wagon.” Lambert was backed by her band, along with a string section wearing black cowboy hats to mirror that of the entertainer: Lambert, in a black hat, wore a black dress adorned with blue fames. She also received an assist from an army of Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, who delivered their choreographed routine as Lambert sang.

entertainment.title: Taylor Swift’s guitar teacher defends hit piece writer: Positive comments ‘probably died in the editing room’
entertainment.summary: The guitar teacher said he is proud "beyond belief" of Swift's career, and wishes his role in the piece was more positive.
entertainment.body:
Swifties will have to wait for (Taylor’s Version) to read nice things about their beloved pop star.

Taylor Swift’s former guitar teacher, Ronnie Cremer, who participated in Vanity Fair’s “The Mastermind” feature, isn’t blaming writer May Jeong for the negative angle — he believes her editors had it out for the singer.

“What I think happened, and I have no evidence of this, but I think it probably died in the editing room,” Cremer told Page Six. “May had tons of information, and a lot of the information I gave her did not make it into the story, and I was a little disappointed by that.”

“She told me that the editors were giving her a difficult time over certain comments,” Cremer added. “And I didn’t quite understand what that means, but there was not much I could do about it.”

The article, considered by many to be a hit piece, highlighted a story Cremer previously shared with the New York Daily News about when Swift’s mom, Andrea, gave her a salad while the rest of the family ate Taco Bell, allegedly saying, “Nobody wants to see a fat pop star.”

That one quote made headlines, but Cremer said the majority of his conversations with Jeong were positive as he detailed his time with the Swifts from 2004 to 2006.

“I wasn’t trying to bash Taylor,” the guitar teacher continued. “I mean, that’s all played out already. We don’t need more negativity in the world. So, I thought if I can help in a positive way, I’ll answer brutally honest questions.”

“I’m not afraid to answer those questions, and I was hoping that they would have used more of those answers, but the magazine chose a different path,” he added.

entertainment.title: Paige DeSorbo Goes Social Media Official With Boyfriend Joe D’Amelio
entertainment.summary: Paige DeSorbo is serving up a hard launch. Four months after the Summer House alum denied rumors that she and boyfriend Joe D’Amelio got engaged, she made their romance social media official,...
entertainment.body:
Four months after the Summer House alum denied rumors that she and boyfriend Joe D’Amelio got engaged, she made their romance social media official, sharing a funny video on TikTok of her friends making homemade pizzas.

As DeSorbo captioned the Nov. 25 TikTok video, which she also shared on her Instagram Stories, “We aren’t Italian at all.”

The clip featured the Giggly Squad podcast host’s pals cooking up pies and hanging out as they lip-synced to audio from a scene from the 1990 classic Goodfellas , in which Henry Hill ( Ray Liotta ) introduces the members of mafia capo Paulie Cicero ’s crew.

“There was Jimmy, and Tommy, and me. And there was Anthony Stabile, Frankie Carbone,” Liotta’s Hill says in the scene. “And then there was Mo Black’s brother, Fat Andy and his guys, Frankie the Wop and Freddy No Nose. And then there was Pete the Killer, who was Sally Balls’ brother. Then you had Nickey Eyes and Mikey Franzese.”

And among the family and friends who made a cameo in DeSorbo’s video was D’Amelio, who lifted up his drink in greeting as the camera panned to him during the “Nickey Eyes” line.

While the couple first sparked romance rumors way back in February 2025, they have kept their relationship offline until now. And fans couldn’t help but get excited about the update.

“GIRRRRRRRRL it’s tiktok official okayyy honey,” one user wrote in the comments section of DeSorbo’s video, while another added, “Paige he’s so handsome and fits in so well I’m so happy for you kween.”

Although this marks the D’Amelio’s debut on DeSorbo’s social media, the Bravo alum previously shared insight into their romance, joking to Us Weekly in a February interview that while Italian men have a reputation for being “not quiet,” she’s found that’s not the case.

entertainment.body:
Lana Del Rey is giving fans an update on her long-awaited new music.

In a Thanksgiving Day Instagram post on Thursday (Nov. 26), the alt-pop singer-songwriter revealed that her upcoming country album, Stove , and its companion album, Spyda , are “definitely getting close to wrapping up.”

“The albums are coming along so well. I’m happy with them,” Del Rey wrote alongside a photo gallery. “Taking time cooking but definitely gonna be out at the perfect time considering how much music is on both of them. Although Del Rey didn’t reveal a release date for either project, she offered insight into the albums’ evolution.

“It’s an unusual coupling of albums that explain where I started when I announced everything 4 years ago to my perspective now on my internal web of people and their reactions to my happiness and physical growth and success,” she wrote.

Del Rey also offered insight into the albums’ introspective themes, referencing what may be a song titled “You’ve Got a Friend.” She described its lyrics as containing substantial “internal dialogue” about the events of the past several years, the lessons she’s learned, and whether everything happens on “God’s time.”

“Makes me feel like there’s no way the things that happen could be random – one thing that comes to mind is that little quote… You can have it all, but you can’t have it all at the same time,” she wrote.
