entertainment.summary: A new couple emerges in Season 2 of The Hunting Wives, even if the Netflix drama's creator tells TVLine it wasn't part of her original plan.
entertainment.body:
Netflix Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Warning: This article spoils Season 2, Episode 5 of Netflix's "The Hunting Wives." Proceed with caution.

Released on Thanksgiving, the second season of Netflix's "The Hunting Wives" gives patient fans plenty to be thankful for, with more twists, more turns, and, of course, more pegging. For now, we're specifically raising our glass to a juicy reveal in Episode 5, confirming that two beloved characters are even more fond of each other than the fans are of them.

We're talking, of course, about Deputy Wanda Salazar (Karen Rodriguez) and Deputy Walter Flynn (Hunter Emery), both of whom were promoted to series regulars for Season 2. We learn through a flashback in Episode 5 that Flynn and Salazar have been secretly hooking up for at least two months, much to the delight of their shippers.

"It's so funny, my original pitch for Season 2 to Netflix was that we would reveal that [Flynn and Salazar] had slept together, but they would not end up together because she's the only character in the show that puts her job first and has a real moral compass," series creator Rebecca Perry Cutter tells TVLine. "But once I saw the chemistry, I was like, no, f*** that."

And thank goodness Cutter decided against her original plan, because Flynn and Salazar's romance provides a much-needed bright spot in a season otherwise jam-packed with death, deceit, and general devastation. She sits by his side when a shoot-out with Zelda's thugs leaves him comatose, and he stands by her side at the end of the season when... well, we won't give that away for those who haven't finished their binge yet.

Netflix But as much as Rebecca Perry Cutter loves the relationship that Flynn and Salazar bring to "The Hunting Wives" Season 2 , they aren't her favorite couple on the Netflix drama. No, that honor — as surprising as it may sound to some readers — goes to Callie (Jaime Ray Newman) and Sheriff Jonny (Branton Box), both of whom engage in quite a bit of extramarital fun this year.

"I still maintain that Callie and Jonny have the best marriage on the show," Cutter tells TVLine. "The joy about doing this show, about sexuality and queer sexuality in this repressed red town, is that we don't have to define things the way you would define them in the big city. So I don't know, what does he call himself? I don't get to decide that. It's sort of mystery, and I love the mystery of it, and I love Callie and Johnny together."

“I feel like that’s what happens when you only have one client,” Simone, 38, said. “Why do you have so much time to be in everybody else’s business?”

Simone — who joined the show as a “friend of” midway through Season 16 and previously starred in “The Real World: Brooklyn” — claimed Toye is always “doing the most” at cast events.

For instance, in an unseen moment that aired during the “RHONY: After Show,” Toye tracked De Silva’s location and crashed her lunch with Simone unannounced.

“You will find a recurring theme of her needing attention,” Simone said. “Look, we all love attention. Hell, I’ve done three reality shows. But at a certain point, the well runs dry. Get it from some other places.”

Toye has been facing backlash for her behavior in recent “RHONY” episodes. While she started the season strong with Stewart by her side, the makeup artist’s complaints about co-star Erika Hammond’s private island and De Silva’s supermarket sushi — despite living in a rent-controlled apartment with popcorn ceilings — have made her quite a polarizing reality star.

entertainment.title: One Actor From The Body Is Also In Josh Hartnett's Nautical Netflix Monster Series
entertainment.summary: From a spooky Catholic school to the farthest reaches of the open ocean, genre television can take you anywhere - something this actor knows all too well.
entertainment.body:
Netflix Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover If you've seen the 2026 psychological teen drama "The Body" on Netflix , you may have noticed a character with a screen presence as impressive as his red beard. Canadian actor Josh Cruddas plays Pastor Caleb, a local religious figure and late father to one of the series protagonists, Lisbeth Anderson (Geena Meszaros). Though he only shows up in five of the show's eight episodes, his presence is one of the driving forces behind Lisbeth's actions.

Cruddas also starred in the Josh Hartnett-led series, "Below," which streamed a month earlier on Netflix. "Below" is a show with Stephen King vibes , centering a remote Newfoundland town where the locals are plagued by a mysterious sea creature. Here, fisherman Calvin Penney (Josh Hartnett) must protect his family from the fallout of the creature's presence. Cruddas appears in four of the eight episodes, playing a loan shark named Connor Kopecko who's out to collect a debt from Calvin's youngest son, Jay Penney (Rohan Campbell).

Cruddas's portrayal of both characters involve some genre bending of horror, mystery, suspense, and comedy. "I'm a little scaredy pants, so my consumption of [genre] content is quite limited," Cruddas told Popternative in October 2026. "I just bring [myself to each role]. I've noticed that I gotta have a schtick sometimes, [but] I hope I'm doing every character justice. I try to bring new stuff, but also, you're gonna get a ginger with a beard, no matter what."

Netflix In addition to "The Body" and "Below," Cruddas has a number of other notable film and TV roles to his name, such as that of Fred Waite in the 2022's true-story Western "Billy the Kid," and Miles Miller in "Revival," another 2025 horror-mystery series that's streaming on Netflix.

Cruddas also makes waves off screen as a decorated coach and teacher in the musical theater space. He has over a decade of coaching experience, which includes a faculty member position at the Musical Arts Academy in Ontario, and he's an in-demand private acting and singing instructor for young kids. He also received a 2019 Best Acting Teacher nomination in the internationally recognized Stagecoach Performing Arts school.

Cruddas has pointed to his theater background and teaching experience as something he's consistently drawn from while acting — not only to make his own screen characters feel distinct, but to help young actors who have aspirations of being in a series one day. "I consider [teaching singing and acting] to be just as rewarding and important as any of the other work I do," he told Close-up in 2019. "I remember how much performing impacted my life for the better as a child and teen, and the people who inspired me. If I can bring even a fraction of that joy to the young folks I teach, I'm happy."

entertainment.title: Gerald R. Molen, Oscar-Winning Producer on ‘Schindler’s List,’ Dies at 91
entertainment.summary: He also worked with Steven Spielberg on ‘Jurassic Park,’ ‘Minority Report,’ ‘The Color Purple’ and ‘Twister’ and headed production at Amblin Entertainment.
entertainment.body:
Gerald R. Molen, the Oscar-winning producer who teamed with Steven Spielberg on films including Schindler’s List , Jurassic Park and Minority Report , has died. He was 91.

A longtime resident of Bigfork, Montana, Molen died Monday, his great-niece Rachel Lorraine Pullan announced .

Molen first worked with Spielberg as a unit production manager on The Color Purple (1985), after which the filmmaker offered him his first producing gig, as an associate producer on *batteries not included (1987). Related Stories Music Andy Taylor, Duran Duran Guitarist, Dies at 65 Lifestyle Veruschka, Mesmerizing Supermodel of the 1960s and '70s, Dies at 87

After serving as a producer on the Spielberg-directed Hook (1991), Molen was named head of production at Spielberg’s Amblin Entertainment, where he shepherded such films as The Flintstones (1994), The Little Rascals (1994), Little Giants (1994), Casper (1995), Twister (1996) and the Spielberg-directed sequel The Lost World: Jurassic Park (1997).

“It was the best job in Hollywood,” he said in a 2023 interview, “because any movie [Spielberg] directed I got to produce, and any movie the company did I got to oversee.”

He shared the best picture Oscar for Schindler’s List (1993) with Spielberg and Branko Lustig.

Molen’s producing credits outside of Spielberg and Amblin included the best picture winner Rain Man (1988), Days of Thunder (1990), The Other Side of Heaven (2001), Just Like Heaven (2005), The Meg (2018) and Meg 2: The Trench (2023).

Gerald Robert Molen was born on Jan. 6, 1935, in Great Falls, Montana. He and his family moved to North Hollywood in 1947, and his parents, Gerald Sr. and Edith, built a cafe across the street from Republic Pictures in Studio City.

entertainment.title: ‘Hejira’ at 50: Beck, Cameron Crowe, Clairo, and More Honor Joni Mitchell’s 1976 Masterpiece
entertainment.summary: Jamie Lee Curtis, producer Nigel Godrich, Fleet Foxes' Robin Pecknold, and more discuss the road-trip classic
entertainment.body:
J oni Mitchell wanted to go ice skating. It was February 1976, and she was standing on the edge of a frozen Lake Mendota in Madison, Wisconsin, wearing a black ermine cape and a black wool hat. All she needed were black skates to match. “I had a hell of a time getting the guy to give me black skates,” she recalled to Cameron Crowe, decades later. “He said, ‘Black skates are for, for men, madam.’ I said, ’No, no, you don’t understand. I’m having a funeral for my dead tour. I need black.”

Mitchell had recently cancelled the remainder of her Hissing of Summer Lawns tour, performing her last show at the nearby Dane County Memorial Coliseum. She was exhausted, battling a cocaine addiction, and reeling from the breakup with her drummer John Guerin, which she’d later describe as “one of the most special relationships” she’d ever had. This was her wake for it all, a farewell ride through the ice — not so different from the “River” she dreamt about skating on just five years prior. The ice was starting to thaw, and there were loud crashing sounds coming from the nearby trees, a sound she likened to “cases of Coca-Cola smashing.” She began to skate anyway, her black outfit standing in stark contrast to the backdrop.

Legendary photographer Joel Bernstein captured this moment, which would eventually appear inside the gatefold for her next album: Hejira . On the front cover , taken by Norman Seef, she’s wearing a black beret and holding a cigarette, stoically staring at the camera (she wanted it to look like an Ingmar Bergman film, she said), as a wide, open road is juxtaposed below. The artwork indicated the mission statement of Hejira — in the same way she skated away on that ice and didn’t look back, Mitchell got in her car and drove. “The Hejira album was written mostly while I was traveling in the car,” she told Crowe, in her 1979 Rolling Stone cover story . “That’s why there were no piano songs, if you remember. Hejira was an obscure word, but it said exactly what I wanted. Running away, honorably.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

Mitchell took three journeys while making Hejira : a portion of Bob Dylan’s all-star Rolling Thunder Revue Tour in late 1975, her short-lived Hissing trek in early 1976, and a cross-country drive she made in a white Mercedes without a license (she’d often wear a red wig in disguise, and go by names like Charlene Latimer and Joan Black). Released in November 1976 , the album is a timeless travelogue of jazz-folk magic, when Mitchell left it all behind in search for more. “I’m porous with travel fever,” she sings on the aching title track. “But you know I’m so glad to be on my own.”

entertainment.title: Michael Giles, King Crimson Co-Founder and Original Drummer, Dies at 84
entertainment.summary: "His unique contribution to the evolution of progressive music will never be forgotten,” the band's label wrote.
entertainment.body:
Michael Giles, co-founder and original drummer of King Crimson , has died. He was 84.

Giles died Monday (Nov. 23), according to the band’s record label, DGM . No cause of death was announced.

“Michael’s originality, musical curiosity and uncompromising commitment to creative freedom challenged conventions and inspired generations of musicians around the world,” the label wrote. “He leaves behind an extraordinary musical legacy, and his unique contribution to the evolution of progressive music will never be forgotten.”

Born March 1, 1942, in Bournemouth, on England’s south coast, Giles began his music career alongside his brother Peter Giles and guitarist Robert Fripp . The three formed the rock band Giles, Giles and Fripp in 1967. The group released its only album, The Cheerful Insanity of Giles, Giles and Fripp , in 1968. The album helped lay the groundwork for what would become King Crimson.

Giles and Fripp went on to form King Crimson in late 1968, joined by bassist and vocalist Greg Lake, multi-instrumentalist Ian McDonald and lyricist Peter Sinfield. The band released its debut album, In the Court of the Crimson King , in October 1969, helping establish King Crimson as one of the pioneering acts in progressive rock.

King Crimson made its live debut in April 1969 and later opened for The Rolling Stones at their famous Hyde Park concert that July. Despite the band’s early success, Giles and McDonald left King Crimson during a U.S. tour in late 1969 to pursue a project of their own.

The pair released their debut album, McDonald and Giles , in 1970. That same year, Giles returned to King Crimson as a session musician for its second album, In the Wake of Poseidon . He also appeared on Epitaph , a live release featuring recordings from the band’s 1969 performances.

Giles went on to build an extensive career as a session musician, recording with artists including Steve Winwood, Bryan Ferry, Leo Sayer, Anthony Phillips, Kevin Ayers, Greg Lake, Neil Sedaka, Yvonne Elliman, Rupert Hine, Roger Glover, Francis Monkman, Andy Summers, Peter Sinfield and the Penguin Cafe Orchestra. He also collaborated with former King Crimson bandmates on their solo projects.

sports.body: Tonight, one of the NFL’s biggest games of the 2026 NFL season plays out in Orchard Park, NY. The Buffalo Bills take on the Kansas City Chiefs tonight for a Thanksgiving Day game in primetime. This is the first time the Bills are hosting a game on Thanksgiving, and it comes against one of their biggest rivals — and what many believe to be the best rivalry in sports today. At 9-1, Buffalo is currently in first place in the AFC and in control of their playoff fate. If the regular season ended today, the Bills would claim the one seed and a bye to begin the postseason. If the current standings prevail, the 8-2 Chiefs would be the five seed, and playing at the Cincinnati Bengals in the Wild Card round. Tonight’s game isn’t isn’t of the elimination variety because there’s a lot more football yet to play, but there’s a lot at stake for both the winner and loser. If Buffalo loses they’d surrender a head-to-head advantage to Kansas City, and sole possession of first place in the conference. While many in Chiefs Kingdom are quick to remind Bills Mafia that regular-season wins don’t really matter, that couldn’t be further from the truth. You can be sure that quarterbacks Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes know how big this game is for their seasons. Will Allen and the Bills take down the Chiefs in head coach Joe Brady’s first matchup leading the team against Andy Reid and Steve Spagnuolo? When Buffalo and Kansas City square off, anything’s possible! However, remember that the weather might have a say in how this one plays out. Here’s your open thread for Bills-Chiefs on Thanksgiving night. As always, be kind to each other — and in all things… go Bills!

sports.title: Penalties and forward progress ruling help Cowboys score before halftime
sports.summary: The Cowboys lead the Eagles 28-10.
sports.body:
The Cowboys’ final drive of the first half was aided by three straight plays: A 10-yard pass interference penalty, a 30-yard pass interference penalty, and a questionable call on which the officials ruled Javonte Williams’ forward progress had stopped before he dropped a ball that Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen picked up and raced to the end zone for a would-be touchdown.

There was no Eagles touchdown because of the forward progress ruling, and the Cowboys scored a touchdown of their own after that to take a 28-10 lead at halftime.

In the first half Williams has three touchdowns, CeeDee Lamb has 57 receiving yards and George Pickens has 49 yards.

Eagles quarterback Joe Milton is playing well, with 145 passing yards and a touchdown, but the Eagles have lost tight end Dallas Goedert and running back Saquon Barkley, and they are going to need something spectacular to mount a second-half comeback against a Cowboys offense that can’t be stopped today.

Walker, 23, was also elevated for Buffalo’s lone loss of the season, a 29-26 defeat at the hands of the New England Patriots back in Week Four. Walker did not
sports.body: The Buffalo Bills have elevated rookie cornerback Kani Walker from the practice squad ahead of tonight’s game against the Kansas City Chiefs. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBillsPR/status/2126065974365569364?a=JrwJuRdchVrsq3LlZlg&s=20] Walker, 23, was also elevated for Buffalo’s lone loss of the season, a 29-26 defeat at the hands of the New England Patriots back in Week Four. Walker did not see a snap on defense during that game, but he did make one tackle on 11 special teams snaps. During the preseason, Walker was outstanding for the Bills. He consistently impressed during training camp practices before playing lights-out during the exhibition slate. Walker had 3 tackles, 2 pass breakups, and 1 interception in Buffalo’s three preseason games. Ultimately, he did not make the 53-man roster, but he has remained with the team’s practice squad throughout this season. He has one elevation remaining before the Bills would have to sign him to their 53-man roster in order to have him appear on game day. With Walker’s elevation, that might give a hint as to the availability of top corner Christian Benford, who missed Sunday’s game with a groin injury. Veteran Tre’Davious White came up from the practice squad to replace Benford in that contest. Joining White last Sunday was linebacker Shaq Thompson, who replaced Dorian Williams at linebacker. Given that Walker is the only elevation, it’s safe to assume that Williams will be ready to roll tonight. Does Walker’s elevation mean that Benford is definitely out? We’ll find out when inactives become official 90 minutes before kickoff, which should be right around 6:50 p.m. EDT. Hopefully, our collective turkey-induced food comas will be wearing off by then, and you’ll be able to check back with us before the game begins at 8:20 p.m. EDT.

sports.title: Bears stun Lions on late Rome Odunze TD
sports.summary: The Bears came through at the end of a wild second half in Detroit.
sports.body:
Caleb Williams hit wide receiver Rome Odunze in the back corner of the end zone for a six-yard touchdown with three seconds left on the clock. The extra point gave the Bears a 39-35 lead and the game came to an end after the Lions’ attempt to lateral down the field failed to produce a miracle.

It was the first time the Bears led all day, but that’s all it took for them to end the day in sole possession of first place in the NFC North. Odunze’s score capped a wild second half that saw the two teams put up 55 combined points in one of the most entertaining games of the season.

The game-winning touchdown drive came after Lions head coach Dan Campbell passed on a 51-yard field goal with 2:22 to play in the game and went for it on fourth-and-4. A pass to running back Jahmyr Gibbs was complete, but he was yanked down by linebacker T.J. Edwards and stopped short of a first down.

Campbell’s decisions on the previous possession will also merit a second look. The Lions chose to have Jared Goff roll left to throw on a third-and-1 while in field goal territory and Goff’s pass behind Jameson Williams wound up being intercepted by Bears safety Dillon Thieneman. The Lions chose to run with Sione Vaki rather than Gibbs on the previous play, which was a curious choice on a day when Gibbs ran 21 times for 205 yards and three touchdowns.

That aggressiveness has been a hallmark of the Campbell era, but the calls backfired on a day when the Lions led by as many as 11 points. The defense coming up with big plays to thwart Campbell’s gambles deserves credit for the ultimate result and so does Williams, who finished the day 30-of-44 for 345 yards and two scores despite losing tight end Colston Loveland to a knee injury early in the first quarter.

Williams proved his mettle in big spots several times last season and Thursday’s win is the latest reminder why the Bears are building their future around him. They’ll return home next week for a date with another division leader in the Jaguars and these two teams will do it again in Chicago in Week 17.

The Lions will try to rebound in Atlanta next Sunday and they can’t afford too many more stumbles in a jam-packed NFC playoff race.

sports.title: Aaron Rodgers clears waivers
sports.summary: Rodgers becomes a free agent.
sports.body:
For the third time since March 2025, Rodgers can sign with any team at any time.

The soon-to-be 43-year-old cleared waivers on Thursday, per multiple reports.

He can sign whenever he chooses, either to a practice squad or a 53-man roster. He can wait until the postseason, if he chooses.

Of course, someone will have to want to sign him. In the 2026 offseason, only the Steelers did. At this point, an injury to a starter on a contending team will be the one thing that could create immediate interest in his services.

As long as that team is willing to risk Rodgers eventually dialing up McAfee for another elongated monologue of grievances. At this point, any other outcome would be a surprise.

sports.title: Jahmyr Gibbs up to three touchdowns, Lions up 35-24
sports.summary: Gibbs broke free for 70 yards this time.
sports.body:
Gibbs broke free for a 70-yard touchdown with 8:20 left to play in the game and the Lions now have a 35-24 lead over the Bears. It is Gibbs’s second three-touchdown game of the season and he is up to 18 total touchdowns for the season.

The Bears could have gone to a 12-point lead, but Cairo Santos missed an extended extra point after Christian Mahogany was flagged for taunting on the touchdown run.

Gibbs’s score came after the Lions forced the first punt of the second half by either team and the Bears will now have to scramble in order to find a way to end the day on top of the NFC North.

If they can’t, their inability to contain Gibbs will be a big reason for the loss. He has 20 carries for 171 yards and four catches for 41 yards as the Lions try for their seventh straight win.

sports.title: Carson Beck remains out of Cardinals practice
sports.summary: It looks like the Cardinals are on track to be without Carson Beck against the Commanders this week.
sports.body:
The quarterback missed practice for the second straight day due to the back injury that kept him from playing in last Sunday’s loss to the Chiefs. Beck made his first NFL start in Week 10, but the lack of practice work points to veteran Josh Johnson making another start for a team he joined in the last month.

Guard Jon Gaines (ankle) and linebacker Josh Sweat (rest, shoulder) were also out of practice on Thursday.

Tight end Hunter Long (ankle), linebacker Karson Sharar (groin), and linebacker Cody Simon (calf) were limited participants. Safety Budda Baker (rest, elbow), center Hjalte Froholdt (rest), guard Isaac Seumalo (rest), linebacker Mack Wilson (rest), and defensive lineman Zach Carter (knee) were all full participants.

sports.title: Matt LaFleur on Packers' run-game struggles: "We're trying"
sports.summary: The Packers weren't able to stop the run on Wednesday against the Rams.
sports.body:
“Right now, we’re a pass-heavy offense and we’re trying to sneak in some runs there to at least keep the defense honest,” coach Matt LaFleur told reporters after the 26-13 loss when asked about his team’s offensive identity.

“Obviously not, not when you lose the game like that,” LaFleur said. “So I would say the answer to your question is no. I mean, you’ve got to convert third downs too. You’ve got to get those opportunities to get some first downs. And the second half, I think we had one drive that was a seven-play drive or whatever and everything else was like three-and-out or two-and-out and we turned the ball over.”

On a night when the Rams had 241 yards rushing against only 132 yards passing, the Packers mustered only 55 rushing yards on 14 attempts.

Not having Josh Jacobs didn’t help matters. Without Jacobs (who’s recovering from a broken finger), the Packers’ backfield consisted of Kaleb Johnson (eight carries for 13 yards), MarShawn Lloyd (one carry for 10 yards), and Chris Brooks (one carry for four yards).

Receiver Savion Williams ran the ball twice for 18 yards, making him the leading rusher for Green Bay. Quarterback Jordan Love added one for seven, and receiver Bo Melton ran one time, for three yards.

And, no, that’s not good enough. Especially on a night when receiver Christian Watson was lost early to a concussion.

Even if the Packers can muster enough wins over the final six weeks to qualify for the postseason, it will become very hard to win in January if they can’t run or stop the run.

sports.title: Bears back within 26-24 on D'Andre Swift TD run
sports.summary: The Bears and Lions are lighting up the scoreboard in the second half.
sports.body:
Bears running back D’Andre Swift broke loose for a 30-yard touchdown with 3:09 left in the third quarter. The score made it 26-24 Lions and was the third touchdown in three total possessions for the NFC North teams since halftime.

Swift also had an 18-yard catch during the drive and he has 134 yards from scrimmage already this afternoon. Kyle Monangai ran for the first two Bears touchdowns and the team now has 126 yards on the ground on Thanksgiving.

The Bears have shown they can put points on the board. Now they need to show they can make enough stops to make them winners.

sports.body:
The Eagles’ inactives are OLB Arnold Ebiketie, QB Cole Payton, CB Jonathan Jones, OLB A.J. Epenesa, OL Ajani Cornelius and TE Grant Calcaterra.

The Cowboys’ inactives are RG Tyler Booker, WR Jonathan Mingo, S P.J. Locke, TE Jake Ferguson, DT Jonathan Bullard, LB Jaishawn Barham.

sports.title: Jahmyr Gibbs scores again, Lions lead 26-17
sports.summary: Gibbs is up to 17 touchdowns on the season.
sports.body:
Gibbs scored his second touchdown of the game with 5:45 to play in the third quarter and the Lions moved their lead over the Bears to 26-17. It’s the third straight game with multiple touchdowns for the Lions star.

Wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown is another star for Detroit and he made a tough catch to pick up 17 yards on the way to the end zone. He also drew a pass interference penalty to set the Lions up on the 1-yard-line and Gibbs took care of things from there.

The Bears rallied for a touchdown to open the second half, but they’re going to need to start getting some defensive stops to pull off a comeback win in Detroit.

sports.title: Bears cut Lions lead to 19-17 on Kyle Monangai's second TD
sports.summary: The Bears opened the second half with a touchdown drive.
sports.body:
Running back Kyle Monangai scored his second touchdown of the game to cap the team’s first possession of the third quarter and the Lions’ lead has been slashed to 19-17.

Monangai also had a 14-yard pass reception on the drive and Caleb Williams picked up 25 more with a strike to wide receiver Luther Burden. The running back now has five touchdowns this season and it is his second multi-score game of the year.

The Lions will try to put more breathing room between themselves and the Bears when they get the ball for the first time since the halftime break.

sports.title: Lions score nine quick points before halftime, lead Bears 19-10
sports.summary: A safety and a touchdown have the home team up after 30 minutes of play.
sports.body:
Defensive end Derrick Moore forced Bears quarterback Caleb Williams to fumble on a sack in the end zone and Bears tackle Darnell Wright was flagged for batting the ball back into the field of play. That’s a safety and Lions head coach Dan Campbell opted to accept that rather than decline the penalty and take the ball on the Chicago 14-yard-line.

That choice paid off with more points for the Lions. Jared Goff and Jameson Williams hooked up for a 39-yard gain to move the ball deep into Bears territory and Goff found tight end Sam LaPorta for an 11-yard touchdown with six seconds to play in the half. That pushed Detroit’s lead to 19-10 at halftime.

The Bears will get the ball coming out of the locker room, but the two scores make for a big swing in momentum after the Bears erased a 10-point deficit earlier in the second quarter.

Goff is 13-of-22 for 193 yards and Jahmyr Gibbs has 98 yards from scrimmage. Gibbs also scored his 16th touchdown of the season earlier in the game.

The Bears lost tight end Colston Loveland to a knee injury early in the game, so he won’t be part of any comeback effort that Chicago is able to put together in the final 30 minutes.

sports.title: Steelers activate Michael Pittman Jr., sign Max Hurleman to active roster
sports.summary: Mason Rudolph will have wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. available as a target in his first start of the 2026 season.
sports.body:
The Steelers activated Pittman from injured reserve on Thursday, which sets him up to face the Broncos on Friday afternoon. Pittman had seven catches for 89 yards in the first three games of the season.

Rudolph will also be able to throw to Max Hurleman. Hurleman was a topic of conversation at Aaron Rodgers’s final press conference as a member of the Steelers because Rodgers questioned why the front office did not have him on the active roster.

The team remedied that on Thursday, but Rodgers will not be able to benefit since he was released after far more critical comments about the organization in the wake of his benching on Tuesday night.

Wide receiver Ben Skowronek was placed on injured reserve and the Steelers also elevated offensive lineman Doug Nester and linebacker Jacoby Windmon from the practice squad.

sports.title: Bears tie Lions 10-10 on Kyle Monangai TD
sports.summary: The Bears spotted the Lions a 10-point lead in the second quarter, but they've wiped it out with four minutes to go in the first half.
sports.body:
Running back Kyle Monangai scored from a yard out to make it 10-10 in Detroit. The touchdown capped an eight-play, 80-yard drive that saw Monangai’s backfield mate D’Andre Swift account for the longest gain.

Swift caught a short pass from Caleb Williams and followed downfield blocks for a 33-yard gain. Williams also completed a pair of passes to tight end Stephen Carlson for 30 yards on the way to the end zone.

Those were Carlson’s first two catches of the season and the Bears may continue to look his way now that they’ve lost Colston Loveland to a knee injury.

All eyes are on the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs when they play, which means there’s always room to chat about the greatest current NFL rivalry. sports.title: Chargers sign Jake Browning to active roster
sports.summary: The Chargers' starting quarterback is in the concussion protocol, so they moved to add another healthy one to the active roster on Thursday.
sports.body:
The team announced that they have signed Jake Browning off of their practice squad. Browning signed with the Chargers in October.

Justin Herbert did not practice on Wednesday because of his concussion, which left DJ Uiagalelei to take the first-team reps. Uiagalelei has appeared in one game this season and he went 2-of-7 for 24 yards and a touchdown.

The Chargers placed defensive back Deane Leonard on injured reserve to make room for Browning. He had 13 tackles in six appearances this season.

sports.title: Jahmyr Gibbs puts Lions up 10-0, Colston Loveland out with knee injury
sports.summary: Loveland left the game on a cart in the first quarter.
sports.body:
Running back Jahmyr Gibbs punched the ball in from the 1-yard-line with 12:51 to play in the first half and the Lions are now up 10-0 on the Bears.

The Bears’ comeback efforts will be hindered by the loss of tight end Colston Loveland. Loveland was carted off in the first quarter and the Lions announced that he is out for the rest of the game with a knee injury.

Gibbs is now up to 16 touchdowns on the season and he’s picked up 55 yards from scrimmage thus far. Wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown has three catches for 69 yards, including a 23-yarder on the touchdown drive.

Loveland lost a fumble on the Bears’ first possession and the Lions forced a three-and-out on the second, so the offense needs to get in gear for Chicago.

sports.title: Colston Loveland goes to locker room in the first quarter
sports.summary: A key member of the Bears offense has gone to the locker room with an injury in the first quarter.
sports.body:
Tight end Colston Loveland was checked out in the sideline medical tent and then loaded onto a cart to head inside for further evaluations. Loveland had one catch for five yards, but then lost the ball on a hit by Lions defensive end Derrick Moore. Linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez recovered the ball to end the first Bears offensive possession of the day.

Loveland went to the locker room after the second Chicago possession and center Garrett Bradbury also suffered an injury on that drive.

The Lions drove for a field goal to open the game and remain up 3-0 with under three minutes to play in the first quarter.

sports.body: To say that Buffalo Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau is having a career year in 2026 is quite the understatement. Rousseau leads the NFL in quarterback hits with 29, and is currently second league-wide with 10 sacks in 10 games this season. His current sack total is a new career high for Rousseau — the first time in his professional career he’s reach double-digits in that category. Rousseau deserves to be mentioned in NFL Defensive Player of the Year conversations. He seems to be a good candidate as an All-Pro selection, and is likely to receive Pro Bowl honors. His success comes following a switch this offseason to 3-4 outside linebacker after playing the previous five seasons as a defensive end in a 4-3 system. It’s the first time in Rousseau’s career that he’s played that role as an edge rusher out wide from the linebacker box. When you run through Rousseau’s stats this year, it’s easy to imagine that he’s thrilled with the position shift. In just over half a season to this point, Rousseau has set new career highs in sacks (10), quarterback hits (29), and pass defenses (8); while tying his career high in forced fumbles (3), and remains just four off his single-season-career-best of 16 tackles for loss. When new Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady hired Jim Leonhard as the team’s current defensive coordinator, many were very curious how the former Bills safety intended to implement the attack-based system he espoused. After all, Leonhard had never called a team’s defensive plays at the NFL level, and he decided to make sweeping changes while marching forward with a large group of players hand-picked by prior head coach Sean McDermott. With the benefit of hindsight, it’s now clear that Rousseau may have been miscast as a do-it-all defensive end left to battle it out in the trenches. He played well there for McDermott, of course, but the brand of game-wrecking energy now regularly seen was at best available in spurts with him so deeply tied up in close hand combat against offensive linemen. Leonhard and outside linebackers coach Bobby April III have transformed Rousseau into the sort of player who keeps other teams’ offensive coordinators up and worrying about game plans. sports.title: Art Rooney II expresses support for Mike McCarthy, calls Aaron Rodgers not a "good teammate"
sports.summary: Steelers owner speaks about Wednesday's insanity.
sports.body:
Steelers owner Art Rooney II has addressed the events that resulted in the benching and then the firing of quarterback Aaron Rodgers.

“A change had to be made , and I certainly agree with the change and the way it was handled,” Rooney told Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette in a Thursday interview.

The change was sparked by the notion that Rodgers gave coach Mike McCarthy an ultimatum: “Either let me call all the plays or just release me.” Instead, McCarthy benched him.

It went to the next level when, as many expected, Rodgers scurried to the McAfee show to take shots at McCarthy for missing meetings, showing up late to meetings, and falling asleep in meetings — among other things, including the ultra-embarrassing “1-2-3 Packers!” moment from halftime of Sunday’s loss to the Eagles.

“There’s maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload,” Rooney said. “He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don’t do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that’s for sure. . . .

“In general, I think, historically, what’s in the locker room stays in the locker room. That’s the way it’s always been. That’s the way it should be as far as I’m concerned.”

Rooney also confirmed that the team supports McCarthy, despite Rodgers’s rant and reports confirming the facts underpinning the petty delivery of them.

“I just want to say that I have 100 [percent] confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond,” Rooney told Dulac. “The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.”

sports.body: Thanksgiving Day is finally here, and with it comes a featured course of football all day long. First, the Detroit Lions host the Chicago Bears in a game that should have Buffalo Bills fans’ attention even through their meals this afternoon. It’s a fantastic matchup of two 8-2 teams vying to win the NFC North in what may be the NFL’s strongest division. The Bills defeated the Lions in Week 2 for Thursday Night Football, and they’ll battle the Bears in Week 15 for a Saturday spotlight game in primetime. Many see Chicago as a favorite to represent the NFC in Super Bowl LXI. The mid-afternoon game features the Dallas Cowboys hosting the Philadelphia Eagles. It’s a game with a far different vibe and two NFC East teams with losing records. The Cowboys still have a chance at the playoffs, mathmatically, but it’s bleak at best without winning their division thanks to the quality of teams in the NFC North. This evening, the Buffalo Bills host the Kansas City Chiefs in what should be another incredible game between two of the best teams in the AFC and this era’s greatest quarterbacks in Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes. We’ll of course have a separate, dedicated open thread for Bills-Chiefs in primetime this evening, but for now enjoy this space to chat all things Lions, Bears, Eagles, and Cowboys… and maybe some Turkey Day talk! We here at Buffalo Rumblings wish you all a happy, healthy, and safe Thanksgiving with your family and loved ones. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

sports.title: Blake Corum supplants Kyren Williams as the Rams' top tailback
sports.summary: It's been slowly building throughout the season.
sports.body:
On his 26th birthday, Corum had a career night. Thirty-two carries, 184 yards, and a touchdown. Throw in 21 receiving yards, and he had 205 yards from scrimmage.

“Happy birthday, man,” coach Sean McVay told reporters after the game. “He was on the set of Netflix so we didn’t even get to enjoy it with him. So, I know that kind of pissed me off, honestly.”

Corum’s gains have come at the expense of Kyren Williams. Despite a report that he’s been dealing with turf toe for a month, this week was Williams’s first appearance all year on the injury report.

And while the fact that Corum got the start last night and 58 snaps while Williams was limited to 38 may have had something to do with the toe, as Mike Tomlin says, “One man’s misfortune is another man’s opportunity.”

Corum seized the opportunity on Wednesday night, as part of a very un-Rams-like offensive output that included 241 rushing yards and 132 passing yards.

For the season, Williams has 662 rushing yards and an average of 4.4 yards per carry. Corum has 731 yards rushing with a 5.4-yard average.

Lurking in the background (but soon moving to the foreground) is the business side of the situation. Corum is in the third year of a slotted, third-round rookie deal. He’s making $1.582 million in 2026, and he’s eligible for a second contract as soon as the regular season ends.

Williams is making $11 million per year, on a deal that runs through 2028.

sports.title: The Lions, despite their resurgence, are 1-8 in their last nine Thanksgiving games
sports.summary: The Lions commenced their ongoing resurgence in 2022.
sports.body:
The one win in that stretch came two years ago, against the Bears. That day, Chicago pocketed a timeout as the final 30 seconds or so ticked away, leaving the Bears without enough time to attempt a field goal that would have forced overtime in a 23-20 game.

The next day, the Bears fired coach Matt Eberflus. It paved the way for the eventual hiring of Lions offensive coordinator Ben Johnson, who returns to Ford Field today for the second time.

Last year’s game didn’t go very well. Detroit scored 52 points. The Bears lost the Soldier Field rematch, too.

This year, history takes a back seat to the immediate future. Both the Bears and the Lions are 8-2. The Lions have won all six of their home games. The winner takes control, for now, of the NFC North — and stays within striking distance of the 9-1 49ers for the No. 1 seed.

It’s not hyperbole to call it the most significant early-window Thanksgiving game ever. In many years, the Lions were the punching bag on turkey day. They’re now the ones doing the punching.

For the Bears, the challenge is to prove that they’re Super Bowl contenders. They entered the discussion with their Week 8 Monday night win in Seattle. Today, the Bears have a chance to control the narrative.

However it goes, the numbers should be eye-popping. For last year’s Packers-Lions game, 47.7 million tuned in. It was a new all-time regular-season record audience, until Chiefs-Cowboys later that day shattered it with 57.23 million viewers.

All three games could be compelling today. Eagles-Cowboys got a boost from both teams winning on Sunday. And Chiefs-Bills continues to be one of the top rivalries in the league — even if cold and wind and rain could take more than a little steam out of the offenses.

sports.title: Chuck Clark, DJ Wonnum are inactive for the Lions
sports.summary: The Lions will be missing a pair of defensive starters for Thursday's home game against the Bears.
sports.body:
Safety Chuck Clark and defensive end DJ Wonnum are both inactive after being listed as questionable to play on the team’s final injury report. Clark has a hamstring injury and Wonnum has a back injury.

Clark’s absence could lead to more playing time for Kerby Joseph, who will be playing his second game since being activated from the physically unable to perform list. The Lions will also be getting cornerback D.J. Reed back after he missed three games with a hip injury.

Cornerback Ennis Rakestraw, defensive back Keith Abney, and defensive end Tyrus Wheat are also inactive for Detroit.

The Bears have deactivated quarterback Case Keenum, cornerback Kyler Gordon, cornerback Isaac Yiadom, defensive back Elijah Hicks, running back Roschon Johnson, offensive lineman Jordan McFadden, and defensive lineman Jayden Loving.

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills host the Kansas City Chiefs on tonight, and it will be Kansas City’s first trip to the new Highmark Stadium. Unfortunately for everyone involved, the Bills won’t be able to welcome the Chiefs with nice weather, which could make for an interesting contest in this pivotal AFC matchup. This one is no different, as the winner of the game will put themselves in the driver’s seat for the AFC’s top overall seed. sports.title: After his Pittsburgh exit, what's next for Aaron Rodgers?
sports.summary: As Aaron Rodgers enters waivers, the first question is whether any team will claim the balance of his one-year contract.
sports.body:
Obviously, no one will do it without ensuring that Rodgers actually wants to play for that team. Unless, of course, a team or two hopes to troll Rodgers by forcing him to show up to play where he doesn’t want to play. Like Marty Schottenheimer did to Deion Sanders in 2002.

So, yes, it would be hilarious if the Jets decide to put in the proper paperwork.

The more likely outcome is that he’ll clear waivers and become a free agent. It will give him the ability to sign with any team, at any time.

No clear-cut contender currently needs a starter. And it would make no sense for Rodgers to sidle up to a quarterback-needy also-ran, like the Cardinals.

Some have suggested that Rodgers could join the Patriots, who will be missing Drake Maye while they try to parlay 5-5 into playoff position. His August comments about the Mike Vrabel-Diana Russini situation would potentially be an impediment to that outcome.

There’s a spicy possibility of Rodgers aligning with the Ravens, who still play the Steelers twice. Is he that petty? At this point, it’s impossible to say he’s not.

Rodgers’s best play could be to wait. Let fate decide. Last year, Broncos quarterback Bo Nix broke his ankle late in a playoff win over the Bills. If Denver’s instant desperation caused them to consider dusting off Drew Brees (despite the fact that he can’t throw a football with his dominant arm), they would have surely called Rodgers, if he’d been available.

Something like that can happen again. Of course, a team that loses its starter to injury between now and the Super Bowl would have to want to do business with him. Which means accepting the very strong possibility that, in time, Rodgers will have grievances to air about his experience.

sports.title: Kyle Shanahan on Brandon Aiyuk signing with Commanders: "They got a good player"
sports.summary: The Aaron Rodgers rigmarole has pushed plenty of other stories out of the spotlight.
sports.body:
Aiyuk visited the Commanders on Wednesday, two days after being released by the 49ers and one day after clearing waivers. He promptly signed with the team’s practice squad.

49ers coach Kyle Shanahan was asked for his thoughts on Aiyuk landing with the Commanders.

“None,” Shanahan told reporters. “It was just a transactional thing and it’s good for Washington. They got a good player.”

Indeed they did. That’s why the 49ers signed him to a four-year, $120 million contract only 27 months ago. They could have traded him to the Steelers. They paid him.

It all fell apart after that, perhaps fueled by the lingering rancor of the protracted and contentious contract talks. Everyone hopefully learned a lesson.

Now, the Commanders have a much-needed piece to the offense. A player who can help fill the void created when Terry McLaurin was lost for the season.

And the Commanders — despite being 4-5-1 — remain in solid position to make a late-season run. With seven games to play, they’re two games behind the Giants. The Commanders hold the tiebreaker, thanks to the 1-0-1 record in their 2026 head-to-head competition.

The Commanders face the Cardinals, Titans, Texans, Falcons, Vikings, Jaguars, and Cowboys. The Giants have the Colts, 49ers, Seahawks, Browns, Lions, Cowboys, and Eagles.

sports.title: The clock is ticking on Mike McCarthy's time with the Steelers
sports.summary: McCarthy's future likely hinges on his ability to win games down the stretch.
sports.body:
Rodgers, as multiple former Green Bay Packers are making clear, is destroying his reputation and legacy as a teammate by breaking the fundamental code of the locker room. But he’s also destroying Mike McCarthy’s reputation and legacy as a coach.

For a change, Rodgers’s rant was centered in reality. ESPNFL reports that the things Rodgers said about McCarthy are true .

Which could make it impossible for the Steelers to keep McCarthy beyond the 2026 season.

His only path to salvation is to win. Starting on Friday, when the 8-2 Broncos come to town for a game against a Steelers team that, despite the sudden dysfunction, is 6-4.

It’s really that simple. The next seven games will become the litmus test as to whether McCarthy’s now-documented snoring-and-ice-cream-sandwiches flaws are outweighed by his capabilities.

Of course, the fact that Rodgers rolled a grenade into the locker room on his way out won’t make that any easier. Which could be one of the reasons why Rodgers did it.

Maximum chaos will make it harder for McCarthy to win. Which will make it harder for McCarthy to make it to Year 2. Which will create the impression that Rodgers has been vindicated.

Sure, the initial word is that the situation doesn’t impact McCarthy’s standing. But the most important aspect of Wednesday’s report from ESPNFL that McCarthy “ has the full support of the organization ” carries an important qualifier.

sports.title: Kamren Kinchens: No ill intent on hit that concussed Christian Watson
sports.summary: The Rams defense pitched a shutout in the second half on Wednesday night and they did it without safety Kamren Kinchens in the lineup.
sports.body:
Kinchens was ejected from the game just before halftime because of a hit to the head of Packers wide receiver Christian Watson. Kinchens was initially flagged for unnecessary roughness and the penalty was upgraded to a disqualification after video review by league officials.

After the game, Kinchens said he couldn’t really argue with the decision but that he didn’t regret the play because Watson’s injury was an unintended consequence of trying to make a play.

“No ill intent ,” Kinchens said. “I wasn’t trying to hurt the guy. Just playing football, fast physical football.”

Watson was ruled out for the rest of the game with a concussion and will have over a week to clear the protocol before the Packers’ Week 13 game against the Saints.

sports.body: Aaron Glenn’s first big decision when he became the New York Jets head coach was Aaron Rodgers’ future. Rodgers was interested in returning, but the feeling wasn’t mutual. AG told Rodgers to hit the road, and they parted ways. Rodgers ended up signing with the Pittsburgh Steelers, and that is where he has been since 2025. Late on Tuesday, November 24 NFL Insider Tom Pelissero revealed “The Steelers are benching Aaron Rodgers and naming Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback for Friday’s game against the Broncos. Sources say this was a coach’s decision. But Rodgers has struggled and now Mike McCarthy is making a change.” [Media: https://twitter.com/TomPelissero/status/2125442796467417433] “Aaron Rodgers will be inactive Friday, and now has potentially played the final snap of his legendary 22-year career,” Pelissero added. Now feels like a perfect time to look back and judge whether the Jets made the right decision. In 2025 the Jets finished with a 3-14 record and Justin Fields delivered an uneven season before getting benched. He started nine games, completed 62.7% of his passes, threw for 1,259 passing yards, and had seven touchdowns to one interception. He also toted the rock 71 times for 383 rushing yards and four touchdowns on the ground. Pittsburgh had a 10-7 record in 2025 and made a trip to the playoffs, but ended up losing in the wildcard round. Aaron Rodgers started 16 games last season. He completed 65.7% of his passes, threw for 3,322 passing yards and had a 24 touchdown to seven interception ratio. It seems pretty obvious that Rodgers would have been a dramatic upgrade over what the Jets trotted out at QB last year. Things in 2026 feel quite the opposite. Before Rodgers got benched he started 10 games this year. He completed 60.9% of his passes, threw for 2,241 passing yards, and had a 16 touchdown to six interception ratio. The Jets are getting much better QB play than that with Geno Smith at the helm. Smith has started all 11 games so far this season. He has completed 68.1% of his passes, has thrown for 2,402 passing yards, and has a 15 touchdown to three interception ratio. Seems like the Jets are better off with Smith in 2026 than Rodgers.
